title: Danish word of the day: Sukkergris
full_content:
What is sukkergris?
From sukker ("sugar") and gris ("pig") a "sugar-pig" is not a real pig, but can be a pig made out of sugar.
This can mean a confectionary product formed from either marzipan or boiled sugar into the shape of a pig. The former version, using marzipan, is also referred to as a marcipangris as well as a julegris ("Christmas pig"). This is because a marzipan-shaped pig is a traditional Christmas treat for children, and is often given as the prize to whoever finds the whole almond in the classic risalamande festive dessert.
Sukkergris can also have a more figurative meaning, akin to "sweet tooth" in English: a person with a particular fondness for cakes, sweets, candy, or any other sweet tasting, sugary products.
We're unsure of the origins of this second meaning: did the edible "sugar pig" come first, and the adjective version come about as a description of people who like to eat them? Or does the use of "pig" in relation to a liking for sugar reflect the pig's bad reputation as a greedy animal?
If you know the answer to the above, let me know.
Why do I need to know sukkergris?
Without wanting to get too far into the realms of generalisation, Danes are mostly health-conscious but they do have a weak spot for cakes (don't we all?). Cakes play an important role in birthdays as well as other occasions.
It's common to have a cake at birthday parties, but Danes go a step further by actually taking a cake with them to work (and sometimes school) on their birthdays, to share with colleagues or classmates. In other words, if it's your birthday, you'll be expected to bring a cake into work. If it's not practical to bring a cake or you don't want to, sweets, candies or flødeboller (small marshmallow treats coated in chocolate on biscuit or marzipan bases) will also be well received.
Unlike neighbouring Sweden, Denmark does not have the practice of fika, a daily short break from work during which coffee and cake are consumed. But cakes still make very regular appearances at workplaces.
As such, you probably won't be judged too harshly for being a sukkergris or a sweet tooth in Denmark.
Examples
Danskerne spiser statistisk set flere kager end folk i Norge og Sverige og er dermed Skandinaviens største sukkergrise.
Statistically, Danes eat more cakes than people in Norway and Sweden and are therefore the biggest sweet tooths in Scandinavia.
Jeg spiser generelt sundt og går meget op i min løbetræning, men jeg er en værre sukkergris. Jeg kan simpelthen ikke sige nej til is.
I eat healthily in general and am very focused on my running, but I'm a terrible sweet tooth. I simply can't say no to ice cream.

title: Woman from Zagreb Found Safety from Omiš Fire in a Cave
full_content:
August the 15th, 2026 – A woman named Karla from Zagreb ended up finding safety from the devastating Omiš fire in a cave. “I am so happy to be alive” she stated.
Among the hundreds of people evacuated from the fire-ravaged area around Omiš is Karla from Zagreb, who is now staying at the reception centre at Gripe in Split. Index reports that while fleeing the advancing flames she was injured and lost almost everything she owned, managing to save only her personal documents, reports Dalmatinski portal.
The major wildfire that broke out near Lokva Rogoznica and quickly threatened several settlements around Omiš forced many residents and visitors to abandon their homes in a matter of minutes. Strong winds drove the fire towards houses, cars and the main coastal road, creating chaotic scenes as people scrambled to escape.
Karla described the terrifying moments when the fire closed in on her group. “We were on the road, in the car. At that moment the fire reached the main road. Cars started burning and then we went down towards the sea,” she said. In the desperate rush towards the coast she fell and suffered injuries. With the flames closing in and no clear escape route left on land, she and others took refuge in a small cave by the sea.
“We waited for about two hours in a little cave by the sea until the rescue service arrived. Above us the fire was blazing,” Karla recounted. The group sat in the darkness of the cave, listening to the roar of the fire and the sound of burning vegetation, unsure whether help would reach them in time. Eventually, emergency services located them and brought them to safety.
Although she was left with nothing but her documents and the clothes she was wearing, Karla stressed that material losses pale in comparison to survival. “I’m just happy to be alive,” she said. Her story is one of many emerging from the Omiš fire, which according to the Croatian Firefighting Association burned around 900 hectares of grass, scrub and pine forest before being brought under control. Hundreds of residents were evacuated, several people required medical attention, and numerous homes and vehicles were damaged or destroyed.

title: Man Tried to Defend Home in Omiš Fire, But Lost Everything
full_content:
August the 15th, 2026 – A man attempted to defend his home and all he had been building up since the 1990s in the Omiš fire, but tragically lost absolutely everything to the flames.
The horrendous fire that swept through the Omiš area has left catastrophic consequences in its wake. The blaze swallowed houses, cars and hospitality facilities, causing enormous material damage and creating chaos on the ground. One person tragically died in the fire, while more than 40 people sought medical help. Index/Lukrecija Zderic reports that the scale of the tragedy and the scenes of burned buildings testify to the destructive power of a fire that in a short time endangered the lives, property and livelihoods of numerous residents.
A stroll through the burned area, which according to initial estimates has scorched more than 1,000 hectares, is staggering. Many spent hours defending their homes from the flames, but when the fire became too great a threat they were forced to abandon their houses and flee, some into the sea directly, in order to save their own lives. Complete devastation now lies where houses and trees once stood, and the testimonies of residents best illustrate the scale of the tragedy and the fear they experienced as the fire approached their homes.
“I’ve lost everything i spent my life building”
A resident of Mala Luka near Omiš, Marin Ozretić, lost the home he built in the 1990s. When the fire broke out he tried to defend the house he lived in, but when the flames approached the building itself he was forced to flee so that his car would not burn and so that he would not remain trapped in the fire.
“How can I tell you… I’d been building this my whole life. We had to run. When it started, when it came from above, the flames were more than two or three metres high. I evacuated myself. There wasn’t even a moment of fear, because we were pouring water so it wouldn’t pass. I was watering these pines here, I watered these as far as the hose could reach. And then, after that, when I saw there was no hope left for me, I just had to go. Then I got into the car and at the last moment I saved the car, and myself,” he revealed.
Tourists from the Czech Republic also lost their car to the fire, leaving them still unsure how they will return to their homeland. The owner of the apartment where they were staying, Anđelko Kovačić, lost his house in the old village, as well as the workshop and the boats they were repairing, since he is engaged in servicing and repairing vessels.
Kovačić stated that he doesn’t expect much help from the state, emphasising that a possible compensation of 500 euros cannot restore what he’d been creating his whole life. An investigation into the causes of the fire is still ongoing, and it is not known how one of the largest fires to hit this area in recent years started and claimed one human life. While firefighters continue to extinguish the fire on the hill, residents in disbelief walk around their homes and what remains of them, confronting scenes that the blaze turned into ashes in just a few minutes.

title: Omiš Resident Describes the Fire: It Was Like Being in Hell
full_content:
August the 16th, 2026 – An Omiš resident described the horrendous fire that swept through the area leaving a trail of unimaginable destruction behind it as like “being in hell”.
Index reports that a resident of Čelina near Omiš, Karlo, spent the night defending his house from the fire that devastated his village. One house burned down completely, and at one point the residents were left without water, so they tried to fight the flames with shovels. Children were evacuated to Omiš, while help is arriving in the affected area from all over Croatia.
“it was like we were in hell”
“It cannot be described in words. We were surrounded by smoke and fire. We used water for as long as we could, but our water supply depends on electricity. When the power went out, the water was gone too. Even the firefighters ran out of water, and we continued with shovels. By some miracle we managed to save some of the houses,” Karlo told N1. He said that it was primarily ruins which were entirely burned down in the village. “A house burned here too, that is the worst image of the fire I have in my mind. I don’t even want to mention the body that was found, it’s just beyond a horror.”
“the fire arrived in just 45 minutes”
Karlo said he didn’t expect the fire to spread so quickly. “We watched the light approaching. The fire reached our village in 45 minutes. We poured water all over the houses and that saved us. The night was endless, we couldn’t sleep or eat,” he described. They moved the children to safety in Omiš, while the men stayed to defend the property. “My mother stayed – she isn’t afraid of anything – and she was also watering the house. A neighbour’s car burned in a covered garage.” He admits he was not afraid, but he was fully aware of the danger.
help from across croatia
In the meantime, volunteers from all over Croatia are arriving at the fire site. Among them is Mario from Petrinja, who came with his father and son bringing a donation. “I was sleeping when my wife called and asked if I would drive a donation. I agreed, and I didn’t even know why. Within a few hours we gathered, people were calling, I didn’t even know where I was going. I came with my father and son,” he said.

title: The Night Omiš Will Never Forget – Everything Went Up in Flames in a Second
full_content:
August the 16th, 2026 – The night that Omiš will never forget was one marked by apocalyptic scenes and dramatic rescues from the sea.
An enormous fire that initially broke out in Lokva Rogoznica, driven by strong winds, spread rapidly towards Omiš. The fire threatened houses, reached the Adriatic Highway and forced residents and guests to flee into the sea to escape the flames. The testimonies of the people who found themselves facing the blaze show just how quickly the situation turned into a fight for survival.
“it all happened in a few seconds”
Dražen Ravlić was among the first to warn about the approaching fire. He said he noticed cars starting to turn back from the direction in which the fire was spreading. He immediately warned people at a nearby car park and called the firefighters.
“Everything happened very fast. I went ahead to the parking area and told people to move their cars,” he told Index. Together with a motorcyclist who happened to be there, he tried to help, but without equipment they could not do much. What remained in Ravlić’s memory were the sparks flying, carried by the wind. Afterwards he said he regretted that he could not do more.
Goran Lović, the owner of a cafe near the area where the fire first broke out, described how suddenly the blaze actually spread. “Everything went up in flames in a second,” he said. Lović believes the fire was started deliberately and handed surveillance camera footage over to the police. The cause of the fire has not yet been officially determined and this remains unconfirmed.
cars went up in flames and people fled into the sea for safety
When the fire reached the main road, the road was no longer a safe way out. Some people left their cars and headed towards the coast. Among them was Karla from Zagreb. At the moment of evacuation she was in a car, but the fire reached the road. “Cars started burning and then we went down towards the sea,” Karla said.
During the escape she fell and injured herself. With others she took shelter in a small cave by the sea, where they waited around two hours for rescuers. “Above us, the terrifying fire was blazing viciously,” she described. She managed to save only her documents, but says she is grateful to be alive. People fled into the sea or climbed onto boats they found along the shore. 194 people were rescued from the sea, mainly in the area from Nemira to Ruskamen. Intensive rescue operations lasted from after midnight until almost 03:00.
seasonal workers from mostar fled their apartment with barely anything
Two seasonal workers from Mostar said they fled their apartment with almost nothing. They spent the night in the car, waiting for the danger to pass and trying to find out what had happened to the place where they worked.
The café Mala Luka, where they worked, burned down completely. “We saw it approaching. I told her: “We’re not going to mess around.” We got into the car and left towards Omiš,” they said. Similar testimonies could be heard throughout the burned area. People described how in the dark they watered their yards, extinguished sparks carried by the wind and waited until the last moment before leaving their houses.
“when i saw there was no hope, i had to leave”
Marin Ozretić tried to defend his house as the fire came closer and closer. As the flames descended from the hill, he watered the pines and the area around the house, trying to stop the fire from spreading.
“I spent my entire life building this… When I saw there was no hope left for me, I just had to go,” he told Index. He described flames several metres high coming down from the hill. At the last moment he got into his car and left the area. He saved himself and the vehicle, but was unable to save his house.
Also at the fire site was Anđelko Kovačić, whose house in the old village, workshop and boats he was repairing all burned. Czech tourists who were staying in his apartment were left without a car and did not know how they would get home.
the morning light revealed the true scale of the unimaginable damage
Only when daylight came did the full extent of the fire become visible. Burned cars, destroyed buildings, blackened pines and large areas covered in ash remained. According to the latest information, 43 people sought medical help. Fourteen of them were kept in hospital, and eight were in life-threatening condition. During a search of the burned area, police also found the body of one person whose identity has not yet been released.

title: Rimac: Top Croatian Export Products are Luxury Cars and Battery Systems
full_content:
August the 16th, 2026 – Entrepreneur Mate Rimac has stated that some of the top Croatian export products are now luxury cars and battery systems.
Mate Rimac published on Facebook a table of the 50 largest Croatian goods exporters in 2025, compiled by the portal Lider. Index reports that among the top ten are two companies from Rimac’s business system. Bugatti Rimac took fourth place, and Rimac Technology seventh.
“Croatia’s top export products in 2025 are oil and derivatives, medicines, transformers, luxury cars and their components, dietary supplements, battery and propulsion systems for cars, aluminium foil, food, HVAC systems and pharmaceutical products,” Rimac wrote. This is Rimac’s summary compiled on the basis of the activities of the companies at the top of Lider’s ranking. The table itself ranks companies according to the value of their exports.
Who is actually on the table?
In first place is INA, which achieved 1.23 billion euros in exports in 2025. It is followed by Pliva Hrvatska with 474.4 million euros and Končar – Distribution and Special Transformers with 409.8 million euros.
Bugatti Rimac took fourth place with exports worth 369.1 million euros, which accounts for 94.33 percent of the company’s total revenues. In fifth place is Končar – Power Transformers with 313.5 million euros in exports, and sixth is dietary supplement manufacturer EMPWR with 227.4 million euros. Rimac Technology is in seventh place with exports worth 214 million euros, or an export share of 79.86 percent of total revenues. Also among the top ten are Aluflexpack Novi, Podravka and Klimaoprema.
According to Lider’s data, the 50 largest Croatian goods exporters in 2025 achieved a total of 7.4 billion euros in exports. At the same time, Croatian goods exports exceeded 25 billion euros, of which 21.7 billion was generated by the manufacturing industry.

title: The Croatian River With the Remains of an Ancient City Below the Surface
full_content:
August the 16th, 2026 – There’s a Croatian river which is home to the remains of an ancient city and a 1,800 year old Roman barge. Over 9,000 fascinating artefacts have been discovered at this single location.
The Kupa River in Sisak is home to the remains of ancient Siscia, a Roman bridge and a cargo barge about 1,800 years old, while underwater research continues to uncover new traces of the past. The course of the Kupa River through Sisak today seems peaceful, a familiar part of the city’s everyday life. Putni kofer writes that along the banks there is a promenade and fishermen, kayaks can occasionally be seen on the river, and a few kilometres downstream it flows into the Sava. However, beneath that calm surface lies a completely different Sisak. Over the past hundred years or so, thousands of archaeological objects have been recovered from the riverbed, while underwater, parts of ancient buildings, traces of a Roman bridge and a large river barge that sailed the Kupa approximately 1,800 years ago have been preserved.
One of the most extensive archaeological collections found in European rivers
The scale of these finds is exceptional even far beyond Croatian borders. In a scholarly paper dedicated to the Roman river barge from Sisak, the collection of objects recovered from the Kupa is described as one of the most extensive collections of archaeological material found in European rivers. The objects span a long period of time, from the Copper Age to the Middle Ages, but the Roman layer is particularly rich, created in the centuries when Siscia was one of the important cities in this part of the Empire.
A large part of this collection was not found during classic archaeological excavations. It was brought to the surface by major dredging of the Kupa at the beginning of the 20th century, especially the works carried out in 1912. The monograph Urbanism of Roman Siscia states that the Archaeological Museum in Zagreb holds around nine thousand ancient artefacts dredged from the riverbed, while the Sisak City Museum mentions around ten thousand recovered objects and more than nine thousand archaeological finds in connection with these interventions. Items that at first glance have little in common were recovered from the Kupa at that time: military equipment and weapons, jewellery, coins, pottery, tools and everyday objects. Together, however, they give an unusually broad picture of the people who lived along this river for centuries and used it as a transport route, a source of food, a place of work and a connection with the rest of the world.
Segestica, then Siscia left behind enormous wealth…
The explanation for this wealth lies primarily in the location of the city. Segestica, and later Roman Siscia, developed right next to the river and an important navigable route that led via the Sava towards the Danube. Because of this, the Kupa was much more than the natural border of the city. People travelled and traded on it, a port and other facilities related to river traffic developed along it, and over the centuries objects ended up in the water in various ways. At the same time, the riverbed itself changed. Erosion of the left bank affected part of the area of the ancient city, so structures that once stood beside the Kupa are today partly located within it.
It is precisely this shifted edge of the ancient city that has become the focus of new research in recent years. Since 2021, systematic international underwater investigations have been carried out in the Kupa that no longer depend only on what the river happens to throw up or what dredging pulls out of it. Sonar, diving research and other methods have enabled archaeologists to document what still stands or lies on the bottom. The masonry remains of Siscia’s fortifications that collapsed into the water, large wooden piles connected with the Roman bridge, and parts of lead water pipes that crossed the river have been located. In 2025 the City of Sisak reported that remains of ramparts, bridges and other structures are being documented in the riverbed, so the relationship of ancient Siscia to the Kupa can now be reconstructed much more precisely.
a 1,800 year old roman barge lies in the depths…
Among all these traces, one vessel stands out whose story began long before the current research. At the Kovnica site a Roman river cargo barge was discovered as early as 1985, but the conditions at the time allowed only part of the structure to be investigated. The ship then remained underwater for decades until archaeologists returned to it in the 2025 campaign. A significantly larger part of the wreck, now known as Sisak 1, was then uncovered. The French Ministry of Culture states that the ship has so far been revealed to a length of at least twelve metres, with a preserved width of 3.34 metres, while one of its ends is probably still under bank sediment. It has been dated to the 3rd century, a time when river navigation was an important part of the transport system of Roman Siscia.
The construction of the ship itself is particularly interesting. Archaeologist Anton Divić explains that elements of local river shipbuilding can be recognised on it, as well as techniques known from the Roman maritime tradition. Sisak 1 is therefore important not only as a rarely preserved cargo ship, but also as evidence that different shipbuilding knowledge met and mixed in Siscia.
the home of discoveries from the 2nd century bc
Interestingly, the large cargo vessel is not the only old craft that the Kupa has preserved. More recent research has also revealed a series of logboats – simple boats hollowed out from a single tree trunk. Five of them have been investigated and dated so far, and the results obtained stretch from the 2nd century BC to the end of antiquity. Because of such a wide time span, not all the vessels can be linked to the same period or the same community.
Perhaps the most interesting thing today is that the story of Roman Siscia is not taking place only in museum display cases. Part of the city lies beneath modern Sisak, part of its former edges ended up in the Kupa, and part still remains to be investigated. Over the past century the Kupa has yielded thousands of objects, but its bed has clearly not yet told the whole story.

title: Material Damage Caused by Omiš Fire is Astronomical
full_content:
August the 17th, 2026 – The material damage caused by the catastrophic Omiš fire is astronomical, with the full scale of the damage almost too difficult to cope with for some.
The horrendous fire that ripped through part of the central Dalmatian coastline has now finally been completely stopped, but it has left behind scenes of complete and utter destruction. Houses, business premises, boats and cars burned. Residents are returning to their properties and adding up the damage. One woman tragically lost her life in the fire, but her identity has not yet been officially confirmed, reports Net.hr.
Index reports that the residents of the hardest-hit areas are only now fully realising the true scale of the damage. In the places where firefighters fought the flames, today only the remains of life before the fire are left.
“It’s awful. At first I didn’t have that many emotions, but yesterday I cried the whole way as I looked at it all. I’m not so much sorry for myself as I am for other people. Look around, this is an apocalypse,” said Ivica Marijanović from Čelina. He estimates the damage to his property at between 700 and 800 thousand euros. “This is a catastrophe. It’s terrible,” Marijanović added.
Numerous business facilities were also destroyed in the fire. Boat service owner Ante Kovačić in Vrisovci lost almost all of his property. “Seven or eight boats burned at this location, and I have another location elsewhere where another four were damaged. The damage is huge. Here the work van was scorched, my scooter also burned. It’s a horror,” Kovačić said. Cafe owner Josip Čapeta said that he, his father and a worker stayed to defend the building while others were evacuating. “We stayed here to try and save it. We built this with our own hands and we stayed to fight to the end. We didn’t run,” he said. Despite their efforts, the cafe where eight people earned their living was not saved.
lingering fears will hang around for a long time to come
While some lost almost everything, others find reasons for gratitude in the remains. In the home of academic painter Miro Zovko in Stanići, the fire destroyed some artworks and instruments. “About 16 paintings burned there, there were instruments too. But thank God, my studio upstairs remained intact. And there could have been an explosion from all that resin,” Zovko said. Dominik Čapin from Stanići believes it is a real miracle that the fire did not engulf the entire house. “Today’s Our Lady was with us so that everything didn’t burn. Upstairs it was ten centimetres short of catching the wooden beams – everything would have burned,” he said.
The fear has not disappeared with the fire. Anica Tomić from Čelina described how she was saving a car while sparks were flying around her. “I took a hose from the neighbour and that’s how we were saving things. I can’t talk any more, I’m sorry. Now the panic is hitting me – now it’s worse and harder for me than it was these past two days,” she said through tears.
those injured remain in a critical condition in hospital
While the damage is being assessed on the ground, treatment of the most seriously injured continues in hospitals. At University Hospital Zagreb three patients are fighting for their lives and their condition is unchanged. At the Children’s Hospital in Zagreb, a minor is being treated who suffered burns on 25 percent of her body. She was operated on yesterday. “If everything goes according to plan, she’ll be taken off the assisted breathing device within the next 36 hours,” said Stjepan Višnjić, head of the Clinic for Paediatric Surgery.
At University Hospital Split seven more patients are being treated. “On Friday afternoon we had to operate on one patient whose condition had worsened and re-intubate her. Three patients are on the ward and there are no changes with them,” said Ivo Utrobčić from the Department of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgery and Burns at University Hospital Split.
The fire has left behind enormous material damage and the gravest consequence. The identity of the woman who died is still being established.

title: Omiš Wine Producer: Everything Was Destroyed Within an Hour
full_content:
August the 17th, 2026 – The tragedy of the horrendous Omiš fire knows no bounds as one local wine producer says his next harvest will be set back by about 7 years. He said that the fire engulfed everything he owned in just an hour.
Index reports that the massive Omiš fire destroyed the vineyard belonging to the Mimica family, and right before the harvest. For winemaker Marko Mimica, the fire destroyed in just one hour the plantings he had been investing in for 25 years. This year’s grape crop, which was already ready for picking, burned completely.
“It’s difficult at this moment in time to say anything coherent. Twenty-five years of work and struggle with this hillside disappeared literally in an hour,” said winemaker Marko Mimica in conversation with Nova TV. The harvest had been scheduled for Friday and the team had already been gathered, but the fire interrupted everything. “Everything was pointing to a more than good harvest despite the severe drought,” Mimica added.
a major setback and a long road ahead
Mimica emphasised that the chances of the existing vineyard recovering are very, very small. “Now, as a family we will gather ourselves and try to clean all of this up. We’ll try to get straight back into planting and revitalising new vineyards,” he stated, explaining that this work includes uprooting the destroyed vines, removing the fence and posts, and then clearing and preparing the whole terrain again.
This determined winemaker also thanked his colleagues who have constantly been offering him financial and moral support over the last two days. He is however more than aware that no money can compensate for such a loss. He assumes that a natural disaster will be declared, through which he hopes for state aid as well.
The process of planting a new vineyard, Mimica explains, takes two years. “On this karst, stone and meagre soil it will certainly take another five years until the first harvest. So that is a job of about seven years,” he specified. He took over the winery from his father five years ago and says he has enough strength to continue. He says that by giving up the winery he would also lose his own identity, which he has been building for almost 30 years.

title: Omiš Fire: Rescuers Describe the Fear of Those Rescued From the Sea
full_content:
August the 17th, 2026 – The catastrophic Omiš fire saw many running for their lives into the sea to escape the flames, with rescuers describing the fear in their eyes as they were pulled out of the water.
Hundreds of people managed to escape the rapidly advancing flames of the Omiš fire by fleeing directly into the sea. In their rescue, alongside the Harbour Master’s Office, the police and customs, the owners of more than 20 private boats also took part. Index writes that local residents are gradually returning to their homes in areas where the electricity supply has been restored. Some of them have lost all their property, with their houses, money and all their memories lost to the blaze, reports HRT.
“you could see the sheer fear for their lives in their eyes”
The situation was particularly dramatic at sea, where people were fleeing in desperation into the water from the fire. Among those who rushed to help them was Mario Popovac, who also took part in the rescue during last year’s fire near Marušići.
Popovac and his friends set off towards the location where people were cut off. While sailing through thick smoke and strong wind, they heard shouts from the water. “I stopped the boat and in the sea we saw dozens of people. It was difficult to approach them and pull them out, so we came closer with the stern and then used an oar to draw them towards the boat,” Popovac said.
Among those rescued was a heavily pregnant woman and parents with small children. On the first trip Popovac took 27 people onto his boat, including seven children aged four or five. “The parents were trying to hold their children up, but the waves and wind were washing over them and knocking them back down. The first two or three trips were very chaotic. Later, people called us from the beaches, so access was easier,” he said. He explained that because of the thick smoke they initially could not see the people in the water, but found them by following their shouts. They were floating fifty to a hundred metres from the shore.
solidarity in pure disaster
A large number of people joined the rescue with their own private boats. Popovac mentioned the example of a friend who loaded 20 people onto his four-metre-long boat. Popovac then took them onto his larger boat and transported them to safety.
“You could clearly see the sheer fear for their lives in their eyes. I’m glad that so many people came out with their boats. We all passed each other, helped one another and passed water around. People gave everything they had to pull others out,” Popovac said. Financial aid to Omiš has already been sent by numerous Croatian towns, including Pula, Sinj, Vukovar and Baška Voda. The final amount of damage from the fire has not yet been entirely determined, but it will be exceptionally large.

title: Plenković: Main Tourist Season is Good, We Expect a Good Post-Season
full_content:
August the 17th, 2026 – PM Andrej Plenković has stated that despite challenges, the main summer tourist season is going well so far, with a good post-season also expected.
It’s mid-August and the temperatures are scorching. More tourists are arriving on the Adriatic coast than leaving it, despite the devastating fires that have ravaged central Dalmatia. Traffic remains heavy on most roads leading towards the coast, and a similar situation can be observed at airports located along the Croatian coastline.
Poslovni reports that during the morning hours, long queues of vehicles continue to form along the motorway, stretching from Lučko near Zagreb all the way to Bosiljevo near Karlovac. Occasional congestion has also been reported in the direction of the island of Krk and the wider Kvarner region, indicating continued strong tourist demand even after the traditional peak of the summer season.
Prime Minister Andrej Plenković assessed the current tourist season as better than expected, both in terms of the number of arrivals and overnight stays, and according to fiscalisation data and recorded revenues. Speaking about the positive indicators, Plenković emphasised the broader economic importance of tourism for Croatia.
“This is important for the economy, for GDP growth and for the Croatian economy as a whole,” the Prime Minister said. He added that the government hopes the positive trend will continue into the post-season period, which is traditionally a strong part of the tourist year in Croatia.
Tourism remains one of the key pillars of the Croatian economy, contributing significantly to employment, local business activity and overall economic growth. The sustained inflow of visitors in mid-August, combined with solid revenue figures, suggests that the 2026 season is performing well despite ongoing challenges such as rising costs in the hospitality sector and complex competitive conditions in the Mediterranean market.
With traffic still flowing towards the coast and airports remaining busy, industry observers and the government alike are counting on a solid post-season to further strengthen the overall results of this year’s tourist season.

Ministerio de Ambiente hace llamado urgente para prevenir incendios forestales tras terremoto de 7,4 en Colombia: estas son las recomendaciones
La medida busca evitar una mayor presión sobre los organismos de socorro ante la actual situación de emergencia que enfrenta el país.
Ante la emergencia que se presenta en el Chocó, el Eje Cafetero y el Valle del Cauca tras el terremoto de magnitud 7,4, el Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible hizo un llamado urgente a la ciudadanía para prevenir los incendios forestales y evitar que se saturen las capacidades de respuesta de los organismos de socorro.
Ministerio de Ambiente advierte sobre las principales causas de incendios forestales
En un comunicado oficial, la cartera señaló que en Colombia se estima que el 95 por ciento de los incendios forestales se atribuye a acciones humanas.
Ante este panorama, el Ministerio indicó que "es fundamental que la ciudadanía actúe como un aliado estratégico en la prevención de incendios y en la protección de los ecosistemas y las comunidades", especialmente por las condiciones de vulnerabilidad que enfrenta actualmente el país.
La entidad recomendó denunciar los actos criminales relacionados con incendios forestales. Para estos casos, precisó que se puede utilizar la línea 123 en Bogotá y la 119 en el resto de Colombia.
Además, pidió no arrojar colillas de cigarrillo, botellas de vidrio ni fósforos encendidos en las montañas, debido a que los matorrales, arbustos y material vegetal secos son muy propensos a quemarse. También aconsejó evitar las quemas controladas y las fogatas, pues el fuego puede salirse de control y propagarse rápidamente.
Recuperación de bosques afectados por incendios puede tardar hasta 30 años
El Ministerio de Ambiente explicó que los incendios forestales constituyen uno de los principales factores de afectación de los ecosistemas y contribuyen a la pérdida de cobertura vegetal y biodiversidad.
Según estudios realizados por la entidad, "un bosque afectado por un incendio puede tardar entre 25 y 30 años en recuperarse", un periodo que depende de las condiciones del ecosistema y de las estrategias de restauración implementadas.
No obstante, el Ministerio precisó que, incluso después de la recuperación, el ecosistema puede no volver a presentar las mismas condiciones originales.
Brigadas forestales comunitarias apoyan prevención y alerta temprana
El llamado se produce en un contexto en el que, de acuerdo con el comunicado, se consolida el fenómeno de El Niño, proyectado como uno de los más intensos en la historia del país.
Frente a este escenario, Colombia cuenta con 80 brigadas forestales comunitarias en municipios y departamentos priorizados. El Ministerio explicó que estos grupos cumplen funciones de prevención, monitoreo, identificación temprana y reporte oportuno de posibles incendios, mediante la activación de la cadena de llamadas y la articulación con las autoridades competentes.
La cartera señaló que esta labor permite fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta institucional y activar oportunamente a los organismos responsables de atender las emergencias. Además, la calificó como una acción climática de adaptación y fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de las comunidades, particularmente en regiones históricamente afectadas por incendios forestales.
El Ministerio aclaró que estas brigadas no sustituyen las competencias de los organismos operativos de respuesta, entre ellos los cuerpos de bomberos y la Defensa Civil. Su aporte se concentra en la prevención, el monitoreo y el reporte, en articulación con las entidades territoriales y los organismos competentes, conforme al marco establecido por la Ley 1523 de 2012 y la Ley 1575 de 2012.
Ministerio mantendrá monitoreo de incendios forestales en Colombia
La entidad informó que continuará realizando seguimiento permanente a los incendios forestales en todo el territorio nacional y articulando acciones con las entidades del Sistema Nacional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (SNGRD) y del Sistema Nacional Ambiental (SINA).
Esta coordinación interinstitucional, indicó el Ministerio, permite optimizar los recursos disponibles,monitorear los puntos de calor en tiempo real y desplegar una respuesta oportuna para contener las conflagraciones y proteger la biodiversidad y las comunidades del país.

Explicativo
Las inundaciones y emergencias por lluvias que han golpeado a Buenaventura, Chocó y demás zonas afectadas por el terremoto en Colombia
Las precipitaciones afectan refugios, viviendas e infraestructura mientras las autoridades continúan atendiendo a los damnificados.
El terremoto que sacudió a Colombia el lunes 10 de agosto dejó a miles de familias en una situación de vulnerabilidad que ahora se ha complicado por las fuertes lluvias registradas en varias de las zonas afectadas. En algunos puntos, el agua llegó a albergues temporales y viviendas que ya presentaban daños.
La situación resulta especialmente compleja en el occidente del país, donde las autoridades mantienen las labores de atención a los damnificados mientras enfrentan inundaciones, deslizamientos y afectaciones en la infraestructura.
Chocó y Buenaventura, entre el agua y los daños del sismo
En Quibdó, capital del Chocó y uno de los municipios golpeados por el terremoto, las lluvias provocaron inundaciones durante la noche del jueves 13 de agosto. El aguacero se sumó a las dificultades que ya enfrentaban las familias afectadas por el movimiento telúrico.
La Gobernación del Chocó también reportó afectaciones asociadas con las precipitaciones y avenidas torrenciales. El escenario aumenta el riesgo para las estructuras que resultaron comprometidas durante el sismo y mantiene en alerta a comunidades que permanecen en condiciones de vulnerabilidad.
Mientras tanto, las autoridades avanzan en el registro de damnificados, la evaluación de las viviendas afectadas y la entrega de ayuda humanitaria.
La emergencia también alcanzó a Buenaventura, en el Valle del Cauca. En medio de las condiciones que atraviesan las familias ubicadas en albergues temporales o en viviendas con averías, se emitió una alerta para los corregimientos de Juanchaco y Ladrilleros por inundaciones relacionadas con un repunte inusual del nivel del mar.
A esto se sumó el fuerte oleaje, que incrementó el impacto sobre las viviendas de estas zonas rurales. Las condiciones meteorológicas representan así una dificultad adicional para comunidades que todavía intentan recuperarse de los efectos del terremoto.
Pereira y otras zonas también enfrentan las lluvias
En Pereira, Risaralda, las precipitaciones complicaron nuevamente el panorama. El Hospital San Jorge presentó inundaciones, mientras otros espacios utilizados para recibir a personas que perdieron sus viviendas también quedaron expuestos a las condiciones climáticas.
Uno de estos puntos es el parque Olaya Herrera, donde permanecen familias damnificadas en un albergue temporal. Durante la noche, quienes permanecen allí tuvieron que enfrentar las lluvias mientras intentaban resguardarse después de haber perdido sus hogares.
En Roldanillo, Valle del Cauca, los aguaceros también representaron un riesgo para viviendas que ya habían quedado afectadas por el terremoto. Algunas estructuras debilitadas por el movimiento telúrico terminaron por ceder ante las nuevas condiciones.
El impacto de las precipitaciones no se limita a las viviendas. Las lluvias también pueden dificultar la movilidad y aumentar el riesgo de nuevos deslizamientos en zonas donde las vías y terrenos ya presentan afectaciones.
Autoridades mantienen la atención en las zonas afectadas
La doble emergencia obliga a las autoridades a atender, de manera simultánea, los daños provocados por el terremoto y las nuevas situaciones generadas por las lluvias. En Chocó se han contemplado espacios alternativos para trasladar a las familias cuando los albergues temporales no ofrezcan condiciones adecuadas.
Entre los lugares habilitados se encuentran coliseos, casas de la cultura, hogares infantiles y otros espacios cerrados que pueden ofrecer mayor protección frente a las precipitaciones.
La conectividad también se convirtió en una prioridad en varios municipios del departamento. La Unidad Nacional para la Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (UNGRD), instaló puntos de internet satelital para facilitar las comunicaciones en sectores donde las redes resultaron afectadas.
Así, mientras continúan las labores de recuperación tras el terremoto de magnitud 7,4, las comunidades del occidente colombiano deben enfrentar una nueva dificultad. El agua ha llegado a lugares donde muchas familias todavía intentan reconstruir sus viviendas y recuperar algo de normalidad.

Noticia
Los siete días de horror que vivió Cali: así está la ciudad una semana después del terremoto que partió en dos la historia de la capital del Valle
La cifra de fallecidos en Cali ascendió a 130, con 94 desaparecidos. Más de 4.100 estructuras con daños. Alcaldía pide crear Fondo Milagro.
Una semana después de que el devastador sismo de magnitud 7,4 congeló el pulso de la capital del Valle del Cauca, Cali libra una batalla silenciosa que se mide en las más de 21.000 toneladas de escombros removidos y en el conteo implacable de sus pérdidas.
Se cumplieron siete días de la tragedia y la geografía urbana Cali se transformó. Ahora está en una transición de la fase de rescate desesperado hacia un monumental desafío logístico, social y financiero que definirá su futuro por los próximos años.
El balance del dolor
El más reciente reporte oficial del Puesto de Mando Unificado (PMU), emitido en la tarde del 16 de agosto, expone una realidad dolorosa. La cifra de personas fallecidas ascendió a 130, de las cuales 123 cuerpos ya han sido entregados a sus familias en medio del luto colectivo.
El terremoto destruyó familias enteras como las de Jairo Hernán Saavedra; su esposa, Victoria Caicedo, y sus trillizas, Isabella, Sofía y Ana María, quien fue la única sobreviviente de la onda sísmica implacable que tiró su edificio, el María Elvira Lloreda, en la carrera 58 # 3-158, en el barrio Cuarto de Legua, en el sur de Cali. Allí, ya removieron los escombros con maquinaria pesada y solo quedó el terreno en una esquina, como la huella imborrable de la catástrofe.
Los hospitales de la red pública y privada atienden a 1.485 heridos, mientras que los organismos de socorro —apoyados por brigadas internacionales— mantienen una carrera contra el tiempo para localizar a 94 personas que aún permanecen reportadas como desaparecidas.
Sin embargo, en medio del horror, el pulso de Cali también latió con la fuerza de los milagros que devolvieron la esperanza a una ciudadanía golpeada, como lo reconoció el alcalde Alejandro Eder.
Entre laberintos subterráneos, rodeados de hierros oxidados, láminas retorcidas y toneladas de concreto de lo que algún día fueron edificios de apartamentos y oficinas, la vida logró imponerse.
Esos milagros hoy tienen nombres propios grabados en el corazón de los caleños, como Diana Troncoso y Carlos Esteban Rebolledo, de entre los escombros de Torres del Limonar, entre los barrios Capri y Nuevo Rey, en el sur de Cali, o las conmovedoras historias de los bebés Salomón, de 2 meses, y Maximiliano, de 3 años, cuyos rescates desafiaron toda lógica médica y física. Salomón estuvo aprisionado por el concreto en lo que fueron las Torres del Limonar, dos torres de un total de 34 apartamentos con un garaje subterráneo sobre la calle 10 BIS con carrera 72 y una piscina en la azotea o la terraza. El pequeño Maximiliano fue extraído del ya derribado por completo edificio Cantabria, en el barrio Nuevo Tequendama.
La luz de esperanza la sostienen esos milagros: más de 88 ciudadanos han sido rescatados con vida de las estructuras colapsadas.
Esa esperanza brilló por la solidaridad de una población dispuesta a escarbar entre los destrozos para encontrar vida. EL TIEMPO habló con brigadistas civiles, incluyendo familias enteras que llegaron de otros municipios a Cali para ayudar en los primeros días de los rescates de personas, entre víctimas mortales y heridas. Una de ellas fue la familia de la enfermera y esteticista Carolina González, quien contó a unos metros del destruido edificio Mirasol, en el barrio Tequendama y cerca de la tradicional calle 5, en el sur caleño, que se desplazó con su esposo, quien es escolta, y su hijo ingeniero industrial.
"A donde los organismos de socorro nos informaban que había personas atrapadas, allí estábamos. En un comienzo las labores de rescate se centraron en hallar a las personas atrapadas y luego se pasó a la etapa de la remoción de escombros, cuando ya se tenía la certeza de que no había cuerpos", comentó la enfermera.
Y así sucedió en los primeros cinco días en los edificios Ariguaní, Cantabria y Mirasol, aunque ya en este último el indicio de olores por descomposición orgánica era una señal de que la vida se había apagado en ese lugar, como también en Torres del Limonar que hasta el 14 de agosto había brigadistas empeñados en continuar con los rescates. Torres del Limonar fue una de las zonas con mayor número de personas sin vida y heridas, pero también del mayor número de milagros.
Allí, el sismo ensañó su fuerza provocando el colapso masivo donde, tristemente, más de una decena de personas perdió la vida.
En el conjunto de 16 apartamentos Ariguaní, en el barrio El Refugio, el pasado 16 de agosto continuaban las labores ya de remoción de escombros con maquinaria pesada. Cerca de una decena de personas murió en este lugar, también en el sur de Cali.
Los héroes de la Cruz Roja, la Defensa Civil y el Cuerpo de Bomberos no solo rescataron a seres humanos; la compasión también guio sus manos para salvar a más de 70 mascotas atrapadas, devolviendo la alegría a familias enteras con el rescate, por ejemplo, de los perritos Renata y Antonio, así como una chiguagua de color negro y el gato Pólux bajo las toneladas de concreto de Torres del Limonar. "Fueron días muy duros de pensar que las vidas no se podían rescatar", dijo la abogada Vickye Giraldo, al seguir abrazando a su Pólux atigrado de color gris.
En las calles, el panorama es el de una ciudad herida en su infraestructura. Los equipos técnicos han procesado 4.164 llamados de la comunidad afectada y verificado 763 edificaciones.
El saldo estructural es crítico: 46 edificaciones sufrieron colapso total, de las cuales se verificaron 15, además de que 113 tuvieron inspección por colapso parcial y en 177 ingenieros corroboraron los daños estructurales severos de entre más de 2.300 reportes sobre infraestructuras con averías. Asimismo, más de 530 edificios tienen orden de evacuación. Hasta la fecha, maquinaria pesada ha retirado 21.204 toneladas de escombros para intentar devolverle la movilidad a las principales arterias viales.
Tensiones en el asfalto: entre la emergencia y el malestar social
La normalización de la ciudad avanza a paso lento y bajo un clima de tensa calma. Las severas restricciones de movilidad de los primeros días, que incluyeron la militarización de puntos neurálgicos y toques de queda nocturnos, se han venido levantando paulatinamente a medida que la fuerza pública consolida el control de la seguridad. Sin embargo, la tensión se ha trasladado a los albergues provisionales y barrios populares.
El descontento por las demoras en la distribución de asistencia humanitaria y la entrega de subsidios temporales ha encendido alarmas en sectores vulnerables. Esta presión social se hizo evidente durante los recorridos de evaluación en el terreno, donde el alcalde Alejandro Eder enfrentó reclamos airados por parte de manifestantes que exigen mayor celeridad en las ayudas del Gobierno local.
El dilema fiscal: la ruta de los 10 billones de pesos
Más allá de la emergencia humanitaria inmediata, el gran debate nacional se centra ahora en cómo se financiará la resurrección de Cali.
Tras una reunión entre el alcalde Eder, la gobernadora del Valle del Cauca, Dilian Francisca Toro, y el presidente Abelardo De La Espriella, quien recorrió edificaciones en Cali, en municipios del norte del departamento y en Buenaventura, el mandatario distrital formalizó la hoja de ruta económica: estabilizar, reconstruir y reestructurar la ciudad tomará un estimado de tres años y requerirá una inversión sin precedentes de 10 billones de pesos.
Para dimensionar el desafío, la cifra equivale a casi tres presupuestos anuales completos de la ciudad.
La Alcaldía de Cali ya ha comprometido su primer billón de pesos reorientando recursos propios y vigencias futuras.
Asimismo, se ha solicitado formalmente al Ejecutivo la creación de una entidad financiera especial de reconstrucción o un Fondo Milagro —inspirado en el modelo del Fondo para la Reconstrucción y Desarrollo Social del Eje Cafetero (Forec) utilizado tras el terremoto del Eje Cafetero en 1999— y la renegociación de las deudas de las Empresas Municipales de Cali (Emcali) para priorizar el restablecimiento total de los servicios públicos y la infraestructura escolar y hospitalaria.
Cali cumple una semana de pie, pero en un escenario desconocido. El sismo no solo agrietó sus estructuras de concreto; aceleró las brechas sociales y fiscales de una capital que hoy, entre el dolor y la resiliencia, busca desesperadamente la fórmula económica y política para volver a empezar.

Autoridades del Valle de Aburrá detuvieron en Cristo Rey al procesado por presunto acceso carnal abusivo contra una niña de ocho años.
Capturado por abuso sexual Foto: Alcaldía de Medellín
Un operativo conjunto entre la Alcaldía de Medellín y la Policía Metropolitana del Valle de Aburrá permitió la captura, en vía pública del barrio Cristo Rey, en la comuna 15 (Guayabal), de un hombre de 62 años.
El sujeto era requerido por las autoridades para responder en el proceso que se le sigue por la presunta comisión del delito de acceso carnal abusivo con menor de 14 años.
De acuerdo con las indagaciones de la Unidad Básica de Investigación Criminal Sepro-Meval, los hechos habrían ocurrido el pasado mes de junio y la víctima sería una niña de ocho años, residente de la zona.
Capturado por abuso sexual Foto:Alcaldía de Medellín
La hipótesis investigativa señala que la menor permanecía bajo el cuidado de la esposa del indiciado en el inmueble donde habrían tenido lugar los hechos.
Los investigadores documentaron tres episodios en los que la menor habría sido agredida por el detenido. Con base en la recopilación de elementos materiales probatorios, la autoridad judicial libró la orden de captura correspondiente para avanzar en la etapa de judicialización.
El capturado quedó a disposición de la autoridad competente, ante la cual se adelantarán las audiencias correspondientes para definir su situación legal, respetando el debido proceso y la presunción de inocencia hasta que se dicte una sentencia definitiva.

Noticia
Recuperan en Santo Tomás (Atlántico) camioneta que había sido hurtada al concejal de Barranquilla Alexis Castillo: esto fue lo que dijo
El vehículo había sido robado mientras el cabildante y su familia descansaban en Santa Verónica. La Policía lo encontró abandonado horas después.
La camioneta Toyota Prado del concejal de Barranquilla Alexis Castillo, que había sido reportada como hurtada en el corregimiento de Santa Verónica, jurisdicción de Juan de Acosta, fue recuperada por unidades de la Policía Nacional en el municipio de Santo Tomás.
La información fue confirmada por el propio cabildante luego de que las autoridades desplegaran un operativo de búsqueda tras la denuncia presentada durante la jornada del domingo.
El vehículo, de placas LTV-562, había desaparecido mientras Castillo compartía con varios de sus familiares en este sector turístico del Atlántico. En su interior permanecían prendas de vestir, objetos personales y otras pertenencias que la familia llevaba para pasar un día de descanso fuera de Barranquilla.
Hallada abandonada en Santo Tomás
Horas después de denunciar el caso, el concejal informó que la camioneta fue localizada en el municipio de Santo Tomás.
“Gracias a Dios y a la importante reacción de nuestra Policía Nacional, nos encontramos ahorita aquí a esta hora en el municipio de Santo Tomás, donde fue abandonado el vehículo y donde la Policía, con todo el equipo que se dispuso para poder ubicarla, pudo encontrarla aquí”, manifestó Castillo.
El cabildante compartió además un mensaje de agradecimiento dirigido a las personas que ayudaron a difundir la información a través de redes sociales y medios de comunicación.
“Le damos las gracias a todas las personas que nos ayudaron, los medios de comunicación. Esta camioneta vuelve a Barranquilla”, agregó.
El robo ocurrió mientras la familia descansaba
De acuerdo con lo relatado previamente por Castillo, el hurto se produjo cuando él, sus hijas y su madre se encontraban descansando, situación que evitó cualquier contacto directo con los responsables.
El dirigente político había señalado que la pérdida no solo correspondía al vehículo, sino también a buena parte de los elementos que llevaba su familia para la jornada en la zona costera.
Según indicó en declaraciones entregadas tras el robo, prácticamente todas las pertenencias personales quedaron dentro de la camioneta cuando fue sustraída.
Pese al hecho, ninguna de las personas que lo acompañaban resultó lesionada.
Continúan las investigaciones
Tras recibir el reporte, la Policía Nacional activó un plan candado para intentar establecer la ruta que habrían tomado los responsables luego del hurto.
Aunque el vehículo ya fue recuperado, hasta el momento no se ha informado sobre capturas relacionadas con el caso ni sobre las circunstancias en las que la camioneta fue abandonada en Santo Tomás.
Ahora las autoridades continúan con las labores investigativas para establecer cómo ocurrió el robo, identificar a los responsables y determinar si existen elementos de prueba, como registros de cámaras de seguridad o testimonios, que permitan avanzar en el esclarecimiento del caso.
La recuperación del automotor se produjo pocas horas después de la denuncia pública realizada por el concejal, cuyo principal objetivo era lograr la ubicación de la camioneta y de las pertenencias que permanecían en su interior.

Tres estadounidenses fueron inadmitidos en Colombia a su llegada a Medellín tras alerta de Angel Watch por posible explotación sexual
La alerta internacional permitió detectar a los viajeros durante los controles de Migración Colombia en el aeropuerto José María Córdova.
Tres estadounidenses fueron inadmitidos en Antioquia. Foto: X @ELTIEMPO
La alerta de un sistema internacional de cooperación y los controles de Migración Colombia terminaron por impedir el ingreso de tres ciudadanos estadounidenses al país. Los viajeros llegaron al Aeropuerto Internacional José María Córdova, en Rionegro, Antioquia, donde fueron perfilados por los oficiales de la autoridad migratoria.
Según la información entregada por Migración Colombia, los procedimientos estuvieron relacionados con posibles riesgos de turismo con fines de explotación sexual. Ante las verificaciones realizadas, se tomó la decisión de aplicarles la medida administrativa de inadmisión.
Una alerta encendió los controles
Uno de los elementos clave en estos procedimientos fue Angel Watch, un mecanismo de cooperación internacional utilizado para compartir información relacionada con ciudadanos estadounidenses que pueden representar un riesgo por antecedentes o registros asociados con delitos sexuales contra menores de edad.
Control migratorio en el aeropuerto José María Córdova. Foto:Migración Colombia
La herramienta permite que las autoridades migratorias colombianas reciban información antes o durante el proceso de ingreso de viajeros al territorio nacional. De esta manera, los funcionarios cuentan con elementos adicionales para realizar las verificaciones correspondientes en los puntos de control.
En este caso, la alerta se sumó al trabajo de los oficiales de Migración Colombia en el José María Córdova. Los pasajeros fueron sometidos al proceso de control migratorio y, a partir de la información disponible, las autoridades determinaron que existían elementos suficientes para impedir su entrada al país.
La medida aplicada no corresponde a una captura. Se trata de una decisión administrativa mediante la cual Colombia puede negar el ingreso de un extranjero cuando se configura alguna de las causales previstas en la normativa migratoria.
Control migratorio en el aeropuerto José María Córdova. Foto:Migración Colombia
Una vez adoptada la decisión, los viajeros debían ser retornados a su país de procedencia, sin ingresar formalmente al territorio colombiano.
La estrategia hace parte de las acciones de prevención frente a la explotación sexual comercial de niñas, niños y adolescentes y busca evitar que Colombia sea utilizada como destino para este tipo de actividades.
🚨 Tres ciudadanos estadounidenses fueron inadmitidos por Migración Colombia tras intentar ingresar al país por el Aeropuerto Internacional José María Córdova. Según la entidad, los viajeros pretendían ingresar con fines de explotación sexual. La medida fue posible gracias a… pic.twitter.com/VRgawBO2sF
Con este tipo de procedimientos, los filtros migratorios funcionan como una primera barrera de prevención. En el caso de los tres ciudadanos estadounidenses, la alerta internacional y las verificaciones realizadas en el aeropuerto terminaron cerrando la puerta de entrada al país antes de que pudieran iniciar su permanencia en el país.

MIO en Cali anuncia pasajes gratis como ayuda por el terremoto: ¿qué debe hacer para recuperar su dinero?
Los usuarios del sistema de transporte masivo obtendrán la devolución del 100 por ciento de sus pasajes, hasta el 13 de septiembre.
El sistema de transporte masivo de Cali, el MIO, anunció un beneficio a sus usuarios como parte de las ayudas por el terremoto de 7,4 que afectó la ciudad, el pasado 10 de agosto.
Quienes utilicen la tarjeta débito dale! para pagar sus pasajes en el sistema MIO podrán obtener la devolución del 100% del valor a través de la billetera digital dale!, que devolverá mediante cashback el dinero.
El beneficio ya se encuentra activo y estará vigente hasta el 13 de septiembre de 2026. En ese tiempo, todos los pasajes que sean cancelados con la tarjeta serán reintegrados en su totalidad, de acuerdo con con las condiciones de la campaña.
La idea es que muchos usuarios puedan sentir el alivio y transportarse en este tiempo en el que Cali atraviesa uno de las peores tragedias de su historia, pues la capital del Valle fue una de las más afectadas por el movimiento telúrico.
"Sabemos que muchas familias están atravesando momentos difíciles. Queremos acompañarlas con acciones concretas que les faciliten su día a día", expresó Metro Cali, la empresa que administra el MIO, a través de un comunicado.
Actualmente, el MIO (Masivo Integrado de Occidente) cuenta con uno 850 vehículos afiliados, que son operados por empresas concesionarias privadas.
Hace dos meses, el Concejo de Cali aprobó en primer debate un ambicioso plan que promete 340 buses para reducir esperas y mejorar la movilidad de los caleños.
Se trata del proyecto de acuerdo 096, una iniciativa de la administración del alcalde Alejandro Eder que autoriza el compromiso de $ 330 mil millones en recursos de empréstito para la adquisición de 339 buses destinados al sistema de transporte masivo MIO.
La propuesta, orientada a responder a la necesidad de reposición de la flota y a optimizar la prestación del servicio en la ciudad, contempla que la deuda sea saldada en el mediano plazo con el recaudo proveniente de la sobretasa a la gasolina.

El peligro invisible bajo los escombros: experto explica por qué un rescate acelerado puede ser mortal
Expertos advierten sobre el síndrome de aplastamiento: retirar escombros sin atención médica previa puede liberar toxinas y causar un paro cardíaco.
Remoción de escombros en Cali Foto: Carolina Bohórquez
En medio de una emergencia o un colapso estructural, la desesperación por salvar vidas suele jugar en contra de los propios sobrevivientes.
En las labores de rescate en Cali, la angustia por extraer rápidamente a una persona atrapada puede transformar la intención de ayuda en un desenlace fatal.
Especialistas en salvamento y atención prehospitalaria advierten que acelerar la extracción sin la debida evaluación médica previa no siempre equivale a salvar una vida, sino que en muchos casos puede provocar la muerte instantánea del paciente.
¡Seguimos recorriendo Cali, casa por casa!
Hoy continuaremos en territorio realizando la caracterización de las familias y la verificación de inmuebles afectados por el sismo. Consulta la programación y, si tu sector está incluido, recibe a los funcionarios identificados. pic.twitter.com/xjRfVduEXk
El riesgo varía drásticamente según la condición física en la que se encuentre la víctima. Cuando la persona queda atrapada en un "triángulo de vida" o espacio protegido sin compresión directa sobre su cuerpo, la extracción suele ser directa, tomando precauciones básicas como proteger sus ojos de la luz solar directa tras haber permanecido periodos prolongados en la oscuridad. Sin embargo, el panorama cambia de forma crítica si sobre la víctima han caído escombros o pesadas estructuras que comprimen sus extremidades o torso.
Cuando los músculos sufren una compresión prolongada, dejan de recibir sangre oxigenada. En respuesta a este trauma, el tejido muscular destruido empieza a acumular toxinas nocivas, entre ellas potasio y mioglobina.
🔴El presidente Abelardo De La Espriella nuevamente estuvo en Cali, recorriendo las zonas de desastre por el terremoto de 7,4 del 10 de agosto.
El mandatario reiteró el respaldo a la ciudad y al departamento del Valle del Cauca para tramitar recursos económicos que permitan la… pic.twitter.com/eBzMoXZORM
Si la carga pesada se retira de manera brusca sin preparación médica, la presión se libera y estas sustancias contaminantes ingresan violentamente al torrente sanguíneo.
Al viajar en cuestión de segundos hacia el corazón, los pulmones y el cerebro, el torrente tóxico desencadena el conocido síndrome de aplastamiento, capaz de provocar un paro cardíaco de forma fulminante.
Voluntarios civiles apoyando las labores de búsqueda y rescate en Cali. Foto:Jaiver Nieto Àlvarez.
Por esta razón, la intervención médica no debe esperar a que la persona sea totalmente liberada. Los protocolos de atención prehospitalaria dictan que los paramédicos y el personal de salud deben acceder al paciente mientras aún permanece atrapado para administrarle oxígeno, fluidos endovenosos que protejan la función renal y medicamentos específicos destinados a neutralizar el impacto del síndrome de aplastamiento.
Coordinar la atención médica in situ antes del levantamiento de las cargas es el paso fundamental para garantizar que el rescate culmine en supervivencia y no en una tragedia evitable.

Investigan muerte de mujer de 28 años que fue atropellada por una moto que iba en aparente exceso de velocidad en Barranquilla: dejó tres hijos
La víctima fue identificada como Nini Johana Torres García, quien vivía en el barrio Las Malvinas, mismo lugar donde ocurrieron los hechos.
Las autoridades avanzan en la investigación para esclarecer las circunstancias en las que perdió la vida una mujer de 28 años luego de ser atropellada por una motocicleta en el barrio Las Malvinas, en el suroccidente de Barranquilla.
La víctima fue identificada como Nini Johana Torres García, quien falleció tras sufrir graves lesiones en un accidente de tránsito ocurrido hacia las 9:00 de la noche del sábado en la carrera 7 con calle 96, cerca de la cancha de fútbol del sector.
De acuerdo con la información conocida hasta el momento, la mujer cruzaba la vía cuando fue impactada por una motocicleta conducida por un joven. Versiones entregadas por familiares señalan que el vehículo presuntamente se movilizaba a alta velocidad al momento del siniestro.
Testigos indicaron que Torres García caminaba junto a otra mujer que cargaba un bebé cuando ocurrió el choque. El fuerte impacto la lanzó varios metros sobre el pavimento, mientras que el conductor también perdió el control de la motocicleta y terminó cayendo sobre la vía.
La joven fue auxiliada por personas del sector y trasladada a la Clínica San Ignacio, donde los médicos confirmaron posteriormente su fallecimiento debido a la gravedad de las heridas.
Indagan al conductor
La investigación también busca establecer la identidad y situación jurídica del motociclista involucrado en el hecho.
Familiares de la víctima han manifestado que el conductor sería, presuntamente, un menor de edad y que habría abandonado el lugar después del accidente. Sin embargo, estos aspectos aún no han sido confirmados oficialmente por las autoridades competentes.
Los organismos encargados del caso adelantan la recopilación de testimonios y la revisión de posibles registros de cámaras de seguridad para determinar la dinámica exacta del siniestro y establecer eventuales responsabilidades.
Dolor en Las Malvinas
La muerte de Nini Johana ha generado conmoción entre familiares, amigos y vecinos de Las Malvinas, donde era ampliamente conocida.
A través de redes sociales, habitantes del sector compartieron mensajes de despedida y resaltaron que la mujer había nacido y crecido en ese barrio del suroccidente de la ciudad.
“Hoy nuestro barrio pierde a una gran mujer, nacida y criada en nuestros entornos. Nini Jhoana deja recuerdos imborrables en el corazón de familiares, amigos y vecinos que compartieron su alegría y su vida”, señala uno de los mensajes divulgados por miembros de la comunidad.
Sus allegados también recordaron que Nini Johana Torres García era madre de tres hijos, quienes hoy enfrentan la pérdida de su progenitora en medio del acompañamiento de familiares y habitantes del sector.
Mientras avanzan las diligencias judiciales y de tránsito, las autoridades buscan determinar si hubo conductas imprudentes que hayan incidido en el fatal desenlace registrado en este sector de Barranquilla.

title: Gov’t defends placement of sovereign wealth fund under presidency
full_content:
Assistant Minister for State President, Defence and Security Maipelo Mophuting-Dikoloti has defended government’s decision to place the Botswana Sovereign Wealth Fund under the Office of the President, arguing that its structure goes beyond that of a traditional financial reserve.
Mophuting-Dikoloti was responding to a question from Leader of Opposition (LoO) and Member of Parliament (MP) for Maun North, Dumelang Saleshando in Parliament
Saleshando had enquired why the fund is under the ministry of State President rather that of finance and how were the board members selected among others. In response, the minister said the wealth fund is not only a cash pool but also an asset management entity. “The fund is not only a cash pool but also an asset management entity. If it was a cash only entity, then yes it would be at the finance ministry. But the diverse nature of its cash and non cash portfolio means it will require the convening power of the presidency,” she said. She emphasized that the fund’s placement enables stronger inter ministerial coordination adding that sometimes it may need inter ministerial collaboration as the president may assign. On the issue of appointments, she said the was appointed in line with international standards. “The appointment adhered to the principle of merit, transparency and professional competency as required by the Santiago principles,” she said. Addressing the appointment of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the minister said the process was rigorous and merit based. “The CEO was selected based on his expertise running the largest fund in Botswana. If he can protect, preserve and grow pension funds, then we feel he can also manage the SWF,” she said. On funding, the minister indicated that the wealth fund would not rely solely on cash injections.
“The initial focus is on asset transfer rather cash,” she highlighted. She further highlighted that future capitalization from the fund will include; “ring fenced mineral revenues, dividends from SOE’s and returns on investment, while preserving the principal,” Mophuting-Dikoloti said.

title: Marina receives P300,000 equipment boost
full_content:
As the country continues to grapple with an ailing health system characterised by shortages of critical medical equipment and medicines, a timely intervention by Optimum Health has brought relief to the main referral hospital, Princess Marina Hospital.
Optimum Health, a subsidiary of the Fazel Ismail Group, this week donated medical equipment valued at P300,000 to the country’s busiest referral hospital, answering the government’s call for collaborative efforts in strengthening healthcare delivery.
The Princess Marina Hospital, long burdened by high patient volumes and limited resources, has in recent months faced mounting pressure, with staff often forced to improvise in the face of shortages. The latest donation is expected to ease some of these challenges.
The consignment included emergency stretchers, oxygen machines, wheelchairs, oxygen regulators, surgical equipment, infant reservoir bag silicons, drip stands, hospital beds, as well as fresh fruits for patients.
Speaking during the official handover, Group representative, Fazel Ismail, said the gesture was motivated by a sense of national duty and compassion.
“This is not about me, but about the country. Most of us were born here in Marina and, sadly, for some of us, this is where we will also pass on. Seeing what is happening and reading the news about how hospitals are struggling, we felt compelled to lend a helping hand,” he said.
Ismail emphasised that the donation would not be a once-off initiative, noting that the company remains committed to supporting the health sector whenever resources permit.
“We believe that a better healthcare system directly translates to a functioning economy. When people are healthy, the nation thrives,” he added.
For her part, Hospital Superintendent, Cheniso Siku expressed gratitude for the donation, describing it as a significant boost to their daily operations.
She highlighted the persistent hardships faced by healthcare workers, including equipment shortages and overwhelming patient numbers, stating that such contributions make a tangible difference.
“With support from companies like Optimum Health, we can do much more for our patients. We encourage other private businesses to come on board and assist where they can,” she said.

title: Every child is precious
full_content:
UNICEF, firmly believes that every child is precious, and each drop of the polio vaccine brings the nation closer to a world where no child suffers from this preventable disease. UNICEF therefore, joins the government of Botswana,
WHO, and dedicated partners to mark the launch of polio campaign this morning. The campaign aims to reach over 272,000 children under the age of five, giving each child a chance at a healthy future. "The unwavering commitment and visionary leadership of the government inspire us all, showing what is possible when we unite with a shared purpose. We’ve worked closely with government to facilitate procurement of polio drops, beyond that —we are committed to strengthening the cold chain and logistics systems so that every dose remains safe, potent, and ready to safeguard every child, no matter where they live."
In collaboration with the Botswana Red Cross Society, "we are reaching out directly to caregivers, traditional leaders, and community champions, ensuring they have the knowledge and power to dispel fear and misinformation, and embrace life-saving immunisations." When communities are informed, engaged, and empowered, no child is left behind; every child can grow up healthy and protected. None of this would be possible without the unyielding support of our global polio eradication initiative in the fight against polio.
*Tuduetso Kelapile is UNICEF Ag Representative Officer-In-Charge.

title: Gov't intensifies Ebola virus screening
full_content:
Botswana has intensified Ebola screening protocols at all points of entry following recent outbreaks of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda.
In a public notice this morning, the Ministry of Health said the precautionary move is intended to protect the health and safety of all citizens and residents of Botswana, as well as to prevent the spreading of the virus.
The Ministry stated that the intervention will also help ensure early detection and containment of any potential cases. Under the new measures, all incoming travellers will undergo temperature checks and screening for Ebola-related symptoms such as fever, headaches, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and unexplained bleeding.
“Travellers will be required to provide details of their recent travel history, particularly if they have visited the DRC, Uganda, or any other Ebola-affected area within the past 21 days,” reads the statement.
The Ministry further warned that any traveller showing symptoms consistent with Ebola or reporting high-risk contact with infected individuals will be immediately isolated and transported to designated health facilities for further assessment, testing, and management.
Passengers arriving by air will also be required to complete and submit health declaration forms before disembarkation. Meanwhile, the Ministry has strongly advised the public to avoid non-essential travel to Ebola-affected regions, specifically the DRC and Uganda. The public has also been urged to practise strict hygiene measures, including frequent hand washing with soap and water or the use of alcohol-based sanitisers.
“Avoid contact with individuals showing signs of illness, especially fever, vomiting, or bleeding,” the Ministry cautioned. Authorities have also encouraged members of the public to report any suspicious illness immediately to the nearest health facility or through the Ministry’s toll-free hotline, 16649.
“All travellers entering Botswana are required to cooperate fully with health officials at the point of entry, and failure to comply may result in denial of entry, quarantine, or legal action as provided for under the Public Health Act,” the statement further reads.

title: UB hotel bets on first time job seekers as reopening nears
full_content:
The UB Hotel and Conference Centre is taking an unconventional approach to recruitment by deliberately relaxing experience requirements for most of its vacant positions as it prepares to reopen after a decade long closure.
The hotel, which is managed by Sky Clouds (Pty) Ltd, recently advertised a number of job opportunities as part of preparations for its official launch. The facility has been undergoing extensive renovations.
As per a statement by the hotel, it highlighted that only management positions would require prior experience, while the majority of advertised posts would be open to applicants regardless of their work history.
“This is a deliberate effort to give a fair chance to those who have never worked before. Many young people are locked out of the job market because employers demand experience, yet they can only gain that experience through employment,” the statement read.
The statement added that the hotel would also introduce trainee positions designed to equip successful applicants with practical skills before assuming their roles.
“We will be having positions that are trainee positions where we employ people, teach them the job and then they assume the position,” read the statement. The hotel is expected to employ about 100 staff members during its initial phase of operations. Meanwhile, the facility has undergone a multimillion pula facelift, including complete electrical rewiring, structural restoration, roof repairs, waterproofing, replacement of air-conditioning systems, solar installations and water-heating systems. While the hotel is yet to officially open to the public, its state-of-the-art conference facilities are already operational and available for bookings.
