title: Mortal Shell 2 review: A monumental heavy metal sequel with the spirit of a '90s PC game
source: Rock Paper Shotgun Latest Articles Feed
full_content:
Mortal Shell 2 review: A monumental heavy metal sequel with the spirit of a '90s PC game
Brevs, this one's likely going to be my GOTY
A few hours into your sojourn across Mortal Shell 2's harsh realm of Fainweald, you might stumble upon a tavern called The One Legged Wolf. In a monstrous land inhabited by pasty-faced brigands who refer to you as "brev" right before shanking you, this watering hole exudes novelty. Here, said thugs congregate to make merry and listen to the strums of the shirtless lute-player on stage. Even if you do as I did, and accidentally massacre the guy with a shot from your sidearm, nobody minds. The One Legged Wolf is a weird, memorable place where folk are free to do their own thing.
In many ways, The One Legged Wolf is emblematic of Mortal Shell 2, a sequel that stands out from the pack by melding the modern dark fantasy Soulslike with a willingness to ditch genre formula, a cheeky sense of humour, and the DNA of a PC-only game from yesteryear. The result is a goth cousin of more mainstream fare like Elden Ring, not to mention a phenomenal effort that outclasses its predecessor in a manner that we probably haven't seen since The Witcher III.
Let's backtrack. The first Mortal Shell came out in 2020, and while Ed (RPS in peace) liked parts of it , he also criticised its pervasive jankiness and confounding level design. I can't blame him. I enjoy Mortal Shell 1, largely due to its compact 15-hour size and unique take on character classes, but most people seem to play it for 30 or so minutes before giving up. This sequel requires no prior knowledge of the first game, thankfully, though diehards who stuck it out in Fallgrim's swamps will find returning characters and Easter Eggs aplenty.
More important is the fact that Mortal Shell 2 improves upon every single aspect of its predecessor, making it look like a tech demo in comparison. Once again, you play as a creature who can inhabit the "Shells" of fallen warriors, which replace standard classes. Instead of wrangling with numbers in a lengthy character creation process, the being you control - known as the Harbinger, and a great deal hardier than the first game's Foundling - has a few base stats that go up with each level. The bulk of your abilities come from the Shells that you inhabit, like a parasitic entity wearing a cast-off chrysalis.
Each Shell features its own skill tree that embodies a mix of RPG archetypes, and the first you find will probably be Tiel the Acolyte, a thief who blends into shadows and delivers sneak attacks in typical rogue fashion. Other personal favourites include Proxima, a femme version of the Predator, and Lazlo, a chonky armoured fella who made me say "oh lawd, he comin'" every time I collided with a mass of opponents. Even Sester Genessa, who served as the first game's save system, is back as a playable Shell, and while I struggled with her skillset, build-maxxing players are probably going to love her ability to summon clones.
While the original Mortal Shell only featured four Shells, Mortal Shell 2 boasts eight, and all possess memories that you can unlock by spending a currency called Glimpse. These tangible, character-driven backstories provide a straightforwardness rare in Soulslikes, which are overly fond of hiding their obfuscated lore in a million different item descriptions. There is a overarching narrative at work here, with your Harbinger acting as the servant of an entity dubbed the UnderMether, and tasked with collecting her unbirthed Ova - but it's an affair mostly left in the background. The real crux of the narrative lies in the Shells and the stories behind them, from Tiel fighting his throes of addiction to Proxima finding an unexpected camaraderie with the shopkeeper NPC.
While many of these tales are dark, know that there is actually a wild amount of bleak humour in Mortal Shell 2. What other game features dancing babkas who try to kill you with accordions in the first village you come across? What about the boss who turns you into a sheep, and the other who pilots a rocket-powered mobility scooter like some reject from the Twisted Metal series? And isn't it funny how you start the game with a pretty Midsommar flower crown, and can proceed to put it on all of your Shells, including the big bastard named Gragu?
The number of amusing bits and bobs go on and on, and there's a goofy-yet-awesome flavour to many of them. Take the Troubadour's Lute, for instance, one of the best sidearms in the whole game. You can use it to fire off magical blasts that confuse enemies, or you can sit down to play at any moment if you just want to rock out to sick tunes. This makes Mortal Shell 2 the only Soulslike I know of to actually let you assume the role of a D&D-style bard - and by the way, the Troubadour's Lute is precisely the item that I used to kill the on-stage guy in the One Legged Wolf, whoops.
Plot aside, Mortal Shell 2 also marches to its own beat by foregoing a Stamina bar, allowing players to be as speedy and aggressive as they like. While Sekiro also did this, Mortal Shell 2 doesn't necessarily demand pinpoint parry precision to make up for the inability to become fatigued. Instead, the game offers three different ways to deal with incoming damage, tying each to equippable Seals. There's Guard, which is activated via the Untarnished Seal and lets you block damage at the price of diminished posture. There's Parry, which is self-explanatory, and equipped via the Infinite Seal. And then there's Harden, which is granted by Vatra's Seal, turns your Harbinger to stone, and was the main ability of the first game.
Guarding, Parrying, and Hardening are surprisingly well-balanced. All have the ability to deal Break damage to a foe, opening them up for a riposte, but there are benefits and drawbacks to keep in mind. Guarding is more manageable at the price of less Break potential, while Parrying requires greater timing for better Break damage. Harden is the obvious choice for those who struggle with the art of deflecting an opponent's attack with their own blade, since it potentially lets you forego timing completely and stay in your stone state forever as long as an enemy doesn't hit you. That said, it forces you to monitor a cooldown bar at the bottom of the screen, offering up a different layer of complexity.
Tying pivotal mechanics to items in this manner is unorthodox, and not all players will like it, but I found it a fine way of providing in-game justifications for your abilities. With parrying so prevalent in today's landscape - to the point where it seems pigeonholed into everything in the same way that all games in the late 2000s adopted a beige aesthetic - it's refreshing to be given alternatives.
And Mortal Shell 2 has even more alternatives up its chainmail sleeve, including the Slayer Seal, an item that initiates easy mode by giving you a pulverising punch and your ranged weapons the ability to deal Break damage. Then there's the secret hard mode, which is activated by lighting an item called the Gloombound Candle atop the tower that serves as your hub. The candle turns the world to night, rendering enemies stronger and opening up hidden dungeons designed to test the mettle of more experienced players.
All of these alternatives make Mortal Shell 2 the most accessible and flexible Soulslike I've played, and they've been integrated into the experience in a manner that goes beyond simply being able to call in a summon to assist during a boss fight. Mortal Shell 2 even goes out of its way to acknowledge those who hate the idea of an easy mode by making the Slayer Seal disable Achievements. "It's there for the brevs what need it, an’ for them what couldn’t give a toss about Achievements," the game almost seems to cackle. "But if ye're man enough to hack it in this grimdark world, just go an’ light that Gloombound Candle an’ show us yer hardcore side!"
I'm reminded of how DOOM features similar difficulty options, from "I'm too young to die" to "Ultra-Nightmare." And while modern audiences will probably make plenty of comparisons between Mortal Shell 2 and 2016's DOOM, from the aforementioned Slayer Seal to the way your Shell rips and tears baddies in epic finishing moves, this game made me feel waves of nostalgia for id Software's 1993 original - not to mention the heavy metal-infused era of PC gaming era that it ushered in. I'm talking stuff like Heretic, Hexen, Rune, hell, even Severance: Blade of Darkness.
There's just something about Mortal Shell that makes it feel like a modern descendent of those grim and gritty '90s and early 2000s games, moreso than many boomer shooters. The soundtrack and visuals certainly seem in line with what a modern Heretic might wear, if Raven Software were ever freed from the Call of Duty treadmill to give us one more adventure starring Corvus the Sidhe Elf.
But where this comparison becomes most apparent is in the dozens of dungeons that dot Mortal Shell's landscape. You'll enter these tombs whenever you need to cleanse a save point or investigate a hidden area, and they are delicious nuggets of old-school PC gaming level design. I'm talking enemies perched atop high ledges, secret passageways, archways that you've got to step through to create portals through walls, keys that must be located to open doors. There's even a dungeon that is, I kid you not, clearly homaging the E1M1: Hangar level from DOOM, right down to the shadow line that activates the hidden lift.
Yes, plenty of Soulslikes feature excellent dungeons, but Mortal Shell 2's feel like they might have been pirated as a "top 100 maps" package back in 1998, which is both a sincere compliment and a massive upgrade from the confusing levels of the first game. They are, in many ways, reminiscent of what John Carmack and John Romero might have whipped up at the height of their collaborative years, if only Soulslikes had been a thing back then. And the fact that this game manages to tie retro-feeling maps into an expansive open world that might not be as big as Elden Ring's or Nioh 3's, but is arguably tighter with more interwoven areas, is astounding.
I'm gushing a lot here, but of course there are a few issues. I ran into a handful of bugs on my playthrough, including Sester Genessa's clones missing their attacks more often than not. Stretches of the map need more save points to alleviate lengthy boss runbacks (I'm looking at you, north-eastern Fainweald). It's also clear that Mortal Shell 2 wants you to commit to one or two Shells at most, which might disappoint some. You simply won't gather enough Glimpse to min/max them all, and I expect that many will play through the whole affair as either Tiel or Proxima, simply because they're the two Shells you unlock first.
Still, these problems are tolerable. A patch will likely render the bugs and runback criticisms obsolete, and committing to a single Shell or two is less of an issue and more of a design choice to encourage New Game + playthroughs. This is, in fact, one of the few games that I feel the urge to replay immediately, largely thanks to a desire to experiment with Smert, a badass old warrior monk who can stop time.
Ed recently wrote that Soulslikes have failed to innovate since Elden Ring, and called upon FromSoftware to deliver us from stagnancy. I'm not sure of Ed's opinion on Mortal Shell 2, but in my eyes, this sequel is proof of innovation, and manifests the dream that the developers clearly had with the original Mortal Shell six years ago. Genre standbys have been tweaked, accessibility has been added, and callbacks to PC classics are aplenty - all within a single package packed to the brim with gothic, weirdo charm.
If Dark Souls and Elden Ring are the equivalent of Dungeons & Dragons in this genre, spawning a million imitators, then Mortal Shell 2 is Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay, or perhaps even Fighting Fantasy. An alternate choice - perhaps notorious for its oddball characters and setting where everything is a little bit shite - but one that will delight you with its bizarre unorthodoxy. So take a seat at The One Legged Wolf, pour a glass of moonshine, and stay a while, brevs. That lute sounds mighty fine in the background, and here's hoping you'll take to the stage and rock alongside it. Just try not to rip the poor mook standing beside you to shreds, ya hear?

title: I'm not saying Bethesda are trolling me specifically, but Fallout 4 and Skyrim updates are imminent just as I've modded up the latter for the first time in ages
source: Rock Paper Shotgun Latest Articles Feed
full_content:
I'm not saying Bethesda are trolling me specifically, but Fallout 4 and Skyrim updates are imminent just as I've modded up the latter for the first time in ages
How have I wronged you Todd?
Right, just a couple more location overhauls and there we go. A fresh Skyrim load order created for my first modded toe-dip into Tamriel for quite a while, outside of grabbing the odd article image. Phew, now to relax and sink another 50 hou-wait. Fallout 4 and Skyrim updates are inbound, say Bethesda? Well, that would be my luck, wouldn't it?
On the evening of August 14th, a Friday evening no less, two proclamations were made. Don't do anything stupid and start a wildfire, the UK government trumpeted through the entire population's phones. Not long afterwards, Bethesda issued their own alert. Fallout 4 and Skyrim patches incoming, check your load orders. 'Ah, poo', I said, putting aside the twigs with which I'd been building a large bonfire near dense shrubbery.
The Fallout 4 update's due first, arriving on August 18th and "focusing on general Creations improvements". The Skyrim update's just coming soon for now, with Bethesda promising more info once they've ironed out the details. "As a precaution, prior to these updates we encourage players to log into your game save if you haven’t done so in a while or manually save your load order," the studio wrote. "Once your load order is saved, you’ll be able to re-download your entire Creations list at once when the update is live."
On Tuesday, August 18th, a patch will be coming to Fallout 4 focusing on general Creations improvements.
As a precaution, prior to these updates we encourage players to log into your game save if you haven’t done so in a while or manually save your load order. Once your load… pic.twitter.com/RpZtkHEKqk
Cue many folks getting immediate flashbacks to Fallout 4's anniversary update and the fun its next-gen update caused right before massive mod Fallout: London arrived.
One would hope - and I say that fully prepared to be wrong - that things won't be anywhere near as bad this time around. These creation-focused updates seem pretty small, and as veteran Fallout 4 modder Thomas 'Otellino' Mitchell was quick to point out on whatever you call Twitter these days, mods which rely on script extenders are likely the ones that'll need updating. That's still a headache, given it covers the likes of mods which add new animations and interface overhauls like load order staple SkyUI.
That said, the script extenders such mods rely on tend to be updated pretty quickly following the arrival of a new game version, leaving folks only waiting for specific mods to be updated. That shouldn't take too long either, depending on when modders get time, unless you're running a mod (typically an older one) that's been abandoned by its creator. In such cases, you might have to go without that particular mod.
You can, of course, also stop your game from updating to the latest version automatically. Thanks to all those Fallout 4 updates, guides on how to do it for that game specifically are easy to find, such as this one from Nexus Mods. Personally, I'll just leave Skyrim alone for a few days after the update, then check in to see which of my mods have already been updated themselves.
Meanwhile, if you're taking part in the ongoing boycott of Microsoft-owned games, you don't have to worry about any of this.

title: The US Senate are investigating Roblox for prioritising "revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children"
source: Rock Paper Shotgun Latest Articles Feed
full_content:
The US Senate are investigating Roblox for prioritising "revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children"
Company given till 31st August to hand over key documents
US senators have launched an investigation of game creation platform Roblox on a broad charge of putting money before child safety. They accuse Roblox of being a venue for "sexually explicit (and often violent) virtual 'experiences' with children", and have requested a range of documents and records, including details of the company's collaborations with Sesame Street, the NFL and FIFA.
All that's from a letter sent to Roblox CEO David Baszucki by Republican senator Josh Hawley and Democrat senator Richard J. Durbin, who are chairman and ranking member respectively for the Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism.
"You trumpet Roblox as a safe digital playground for children as young as five," the letter reads. "But the public record raises serious questions about this promise of safety. Over the past decade, police have arrested numerous individuals for committing serious acts of violence and harm against children they met via Roblox, including grooming, sexual abuse, kidnapping, rape, and even murder." The letter includes a footnote with links to some news stories, such as this piece about the death of a 17-year-old after meeting an older man she communicated with over Roblox and Discord.
"Roblox is being used to trade child sexual abuse material, participate in sexually explicit (and often violent) virtual 'experiences' with children, bribe and extort children into producing explicit content, and lure children into in-person meetings," the letter goes on.
The writers point out that in 2025, Roblox reported 65,381 instances of suspected child sexual exploitation to the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, more than double the previous year's figure. "Roblox appears to prioritize revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children," they comment, "and the alleged criminal activity on Roblox warrants congressional scrutiny."
There's an annex with a list of "interrogatories" (that is, questions during a legal action's discovery phase, ahead of the actual trial) and records. Roblox have till 31st August to hand everything over.
Amongst other things, the Committee want Roblox to specify how much they earn from people in various age brackets, from five-years-old to 50 and above, together with how many hours per day and per week those users spend on Roblox. They want to know what percentage of Roblox users aged 18 and under have parental oversight enabled on their accounts.
They'd like to know how much Roblox make use of automated tools for child safety – for example, how many Roblox accounts reported "in connection with alleged sexual exploitation, predation, or abuse of users under the age of 18" across 2023-2025 were assessed by a human. They'd like to know why Roblox's new age verification settings don't apply to bespoke, developer-created chat features that run inside games.
Other queries concern "how Roblox identifies and destroys data that are not in compliance with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act", and "how Roblox prevents an adult from posing as a child on the Roblox Platform to interact with other children". Finally, the Committee want to know how much Roblox spends "on trust and safety for each fiscal year from 2018 through 2025", both in hard cash and as a percentage of their total operating expense and revenue.
As for the requested records, these include an organisational chart identifying those who've worked in "trust and safety, content moderation, or child-safety policy" from 1st January 2016 onwards, together with "all documents showing revenue earned by Roblox from experiences in which exploitation, grooming, or criminal conduct was subsequently identified as having occurred".
Other document requests concern how Roblox design their parental controls, and how they track predators who use multiple accounts. The subcommittee are keen to get hold of any internal assessments "of Roblox’s financial exposure if Roblox made any changes that increase friction on the Roblox Platform, such as prohibiting users under 13 from purchasing Robux or making in-platform purchases". There are more specific requests for documents relating to Roblox's collaborations with Sesame Workshop, the NFL, and FIFA, including details of "the age demographic targeted".
Roblox have long faced allegations that their service isn't safe for kids, both in the sense of profiting from their labour and in the sense of failing to keep out sexual predators. Back in August 2024, Turkey banned Roblox over child safety concerns. In August 2025, Louisiana's attorney general branded Roblox "the perfect place for paedophiles". In April this year, the Australian government declared that Roblox alongside Steam, Minecraft, and Fortnite risk "becoming onramps to abuse, extremist violence, radicalisation or lifelong harm".
Roblox have sought to allay these fears by, amongst other things, rolling out facial age estimation technologies, together with prohibitions on direct messaging for players under 13. The company's chief safety officer Matt Kaufman has sent a comment to Kotaku about the US Senate investigation. “Roblox is built on the foundation of safety,” he writes. “We do not compromise on that commitment. We look forward to sharing the facts about how we work to protect children on the platform.”

title: Helldivers 2 joins PlayStation Plus Game Catalog today, Devoid of Liberty update out now
full_content:
Journey to the Illuminate Void in the co-op shooter to battle mutant threats.
We have watched the Void stretch across the galaxy for too long. The threat posed to our Liberty is too great and we can no longer stand by as the Illuminate gain ground.
Helldivers, you are needed on the battlefield of a new frontier–one more wild and uncertain than any we have faced prior. We must venture into their haunted abyss, the Void, and liberate it back into Super Earth’s control.
Today’s Devoid of Liberty release also coincides with Helldivers 2 entering the PlayStation Plus Game Catalog. Starting today, Helldivers 2 will be available to PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium members.
Journey to the Void
Getting into the Void presents a unique challenge. High Command has ordered reconnaissance missions to gather as much intel as possible in order to give us an advantage.
The planets within the Void’s reach have been altered–strange mutations have left a permanent mark on planets, and intelligence reports suggest that these changes are even more significant the closer the planets are to the Void itself. What lies inside?
Complete new missions
You will be given new objectives to conquer–destroy Illuminate spires and gateways, complete data reconnaissance, and infiltrate Illuminate structures with your team.
New secondary objectives will also become available, from eradicating Void mutations to extracting materials for research, as well as the opportunity to open a secondary extraction zone on the map to potentially evacuate your squad faster.
Exterminate new threats
As you fight your way toward the Void, you’ll encounter new, hideously mutated organisms. We have received intelligence reports that indicate these metamorphosed creatures are emerging from the heart of the Void–they are ghoulish diversions wrought into existence by the Illuminate scourge to threaten our freedom.
The Wretch
The nimble Wretch moves fast and can easily overwhelm weaker fighters and dodge their counter-attacks–don’t let it get the jump on you.
The Crusher
On a relentless death march, the Crusher can take heavy damage and also dish it out. Wear it down before it regenerates.
Dive with more impact
We aren’t sending you in without backup. You may now gain all 300 ranks of security access and privileges, as well as new rank titles.
We have commissioned SEAF platoons to aid in completing operations. They’ll arrive on dropships to fight alongside you and your squad, offering medical support via stims, but also give a boost to your morale when you salute, shake hands, and–of course–hug them.
This is our opportunity to strike and avenge the citizens, SEAF, and Helldivers lost in the Battle for Super Earth.
PlayStation Plus
Join the fight for galactic freedom as acclaimed co-op shooter Helldivers 2 arrives in the Game Catalog – included with PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium*, starting today.
Want more good news? The Helldivers 2 community is about to take on an epic collective challenge: eliminate 500 million enemies by August 18 to unlock four Helldiver PlayStation avatars. Join the fight and help the community reach the goal!
Helldivers 2 Super Merch store
Helldivers 2 Super Merch is now available for those dedicated to the pursuit of Liberty and Democracy. Super Earth recognizes your accomplishments with special merchandise for purchase; complete in-game achievements in Helldivers 2 to unlock this merchandise on the Helldivers 2 Super Merch store**. Want to see what Helldivers 2 Super Merch is available to you? Simply sign on to the Helldivers 2 Super Merch store using your preferred platform.
The latest update, Devoid of Liberty*** is live now! Take back the galaxy, divers–give these squids hell.
*PlayStation Plus Game Catalog and PlayStation Plus Premium/Deluxe lineups may differ by region. Please check PlayStation Store on release day. Digital PS5 games available to stream from your library will vary over time, region, and country. PlayStation Plus is subject to a recurring subscription fee taken automatically until cancellation. Terms apply: play.st/psplus-usageterms
** The Helldivers 2 Super Merch program is currently only available in certain regions. For the full list of supported countries please visit here.
***Gameplay requires internet access and paid-for subscription on console (sold separately).

title: Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Comes to PS5 October 1
full_content:
New narrative expansion, new combat survival mode, and much more.
Update (Aug 14, 2026): New tracks for Watanabe Mode were previously listed here as features in the Complete
Edition, but this blog has been updated to reflect that the tracks are included in the free patch on October 1, even
without purchasing the Complete Edition Upgrade.
Original Story: We are so excited to announce that even more new content is coming to Ghost of Yōtei! On October 1, we’ll have a new narrative expansion, new single-player combat survival mode, and new quality of life updates all coming in Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition!1
Before we dive in, we want to take a moment to thank everyone for an incredible year since Ghost of Yōtei launched. We are so proud of our incredible community, and grateful for all of the fan art, cosplays, virtual photographs, combat montages, Twitch streams, Jubei thirst posts…we promise we’ve seen it all and love to share it around the studio. Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition will launch just in time for our 1-year anniversary, and we can’t wait for another year of new creations from all of you!
In the coming weeks we’ll have much more to share, but wanted to give you a few early looks today at the new content in Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition:
Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara is our new narrative expansion. Split between the present day and flashbacks to Atsu’s time on the mainland, you’ll meet Nagato, a figure from Atsu’s past who has arrived in Ezo. In the present, you’ll explore a previously unseen valley once inhabited by The Snake and his gang of loyal followers, the Vipers. In the past, you’ll experience Atsu’s time in the Battle of Sekigahara and a key moment in her life before she returned home for her quest for vengeance. You’ll meet new enemies and find new heavy weapons, new armor sets, new dyes, and more.
Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted is a brand new single-player combat survival mode, our spin on a roguelike. You’ll accept bounties in order to start new runs, where taking down enemies will earn you perks, as well as unlock additional characters to play as. We’ll have much more to show soon, but as you can see in the trailer today, Atsu is a master with the dual katana, while Oyuki excels with the kusarigama, and Nagato shines with a yari. We love to watch the amazing combat reels that have been shared with us on social media, and can’t wait to see you all try to perfect these runs.
If you haven’t experienced Atsu’s journey yet, you can purchase Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition for $69.99 USD. In addition to Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted, this includes the award-winning main Ghost of Yōtei game as well as Ghost of Yōtei Legends, our online co-op experience with support for up to four players and multiple gameplay modes culminating in a Raid.2 If you purchase the Complete Edition, you can immediately start playing the main game and Legends, and Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted will arrive with a patch on October 1.
Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition also includes all of the in-game content previously included in the Ghost of Yōtei Digital Deluxe Edition, as well as the Charm of Hokkyokusei. If you purchase digitally by September 30, you’ll also get an early unlock of the Sakai Armor on October 1 for Atsu to wear, a throwback to Jin’s family armor from Ghost of Tsushima.1
If you already own Ghost of Yōtei, you can get Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted by purchasing the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Upgrade for $14.99 USD. If you don’t already own the Digital Deluxe Edition and Charm of Hokkyokusei you’ll immediately unlock that content upon pre-ordering. And if you pre-order by September 30, on October 1 you’ll also get the early unlock of the Sakai Armor.
Beyond the new content listed above, Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition includes new photo mode stamps, additional
cosmetics for New Game Plus, and new Trophies for both Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted.
For anyone who owns Ghost of Yōtei, even without purchasing the Complete Edition upgrade, a new patch on
October 1 will add the new Beauty of Yōtei mode, which allows for a screensaver-like view of the environments of
Ezo to keep on and relax at home (and take stunning new Photo Mode captures). We’ve also added new tracks for
Watanabe Mode that will be available throughout the entire game when the mode is enabled. There will also be new
quality of life features including the option to keep an armor set’s appearance while using a different set’s stats, as
well as a new high contrast accessibility option.1
Thank you again to everyone for an amazing year since Ghost of Yōtei launched! We’ll have more to share about Most Wanted and Echoes of Sekigahara as we get closer to launch on October 1, so be sure to follow our social media channels and keep an eye out!
1 Available via patch v.2.0 on October 1, 2026 globally, and October 2, 2026 in some territories, including Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. Internet connection and account for PlayStation required to download.
2 Online multiplayer requires a PlayStation Plus subscription. PS Plus is subject to a recurring subscription fee taken automatically until cancellation. Full terms: play.st/psplus-usageterms.

title: PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for August: Helldivers 2, Kingdom Come Deliverance II, Vampire Survivors, Hell is Us and more
full_content:
Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams and Disney's Atlantis: The Lost Empire join PlayStation Plus Premium.
This month, enlist in Super Earth’s premier military peacekeeping force and fight for freedom across a hostile galaxy in Helldivers 2, shape your destiny in a stunningly authentic rendition of 15th century Bohemia in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, become the bullet hell and mow down thousands of night creatures to survive in Vampire Survivors, or cut a path through lands infested with terrifying chimaeras to unravel the mystery of their appearance in Hell is Us. All these titles and more are available in August’s PlayStation Plus Game Catalog lineup*. Meanwhile, PlayStation Plus Premium welcomes Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams and Disney’s Atlantis: The Lost Empire.
Helldivers 2 will be available to PlayStation Plus Extra members today, August 12, worldwide. All other titles will be available Tuesday, August 18 unless indicated otherwise.
PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium | Game Catalog
Helldivers 2 | PS5
Freedom. Peace. Managed Democracy. Your Super Earth-born rights. The key pillars of our civilization are under attack from deadly alien creatures conspiring to destroy your planet and its values. Join forces with up to three friends and wreak havoc on an alien scourge threatening the safety of your home planet, Super Earth, in this multiplayer co-op shooter from Arrowhead Game Studios. Step into the boots of the Helldivers, an elite class of soldiers whose mission is to spread peace, liberty and Managed Democracy using the biggest, baddest and most explosive tools in the galaxy. They say everything is better with friends, especially when it comes to raining destruction down on the enemies of Liberty! Be warned though: for maximum challenge and collaboration, friendly fire is always on. Today’s launch into PlayStation Plus Game Catalog coincides with a huge new game update. Find out more here.
Helldivers 2 will be available later today worldwide.
Kingdom Come: Deliverance II | PS5
You are Henry of Skalitz, an ordinary man doing extraordinary things, caught in a gripping tale of revenge, betrayal and discovery. Henry will embark on an epic journey, from a humble blacksmith’s forge to the court of Kings, as he searches for purpose in this beautiful but brutal medieval world. From bustling city streets to lush forests, discover an open-world medieval Europe through this thrilling action RPG set amid the chaos of a civil war in 15th-century Bohemia.
Vampire Survivors | PS5, PS4
Hell is empty, the devils are here, and there’s no place to run or hide. All you can do is survive as long as you can until death inevitably puts an end to your struggles. Vampire Survivors is a gothic horror casual game with rogue-lite elements, where your choices can allow you to quickly snowball against the hundreds of monsters that get thrown at you. The supernatural indie phenomenon that lets you be the bullet hell!
Hell is Us | PS5
Intense melee combat meets the thrill of exploration in Hell is Us, a third-person action-adventure game with a semi-open world to explore. Drawn to an isolated country ravaged by infighting, in search of his missing parents, United Nations peacekeeper Rémi goes absent without leave to discover the secrets of his past and deal with the repercussions of a mysterious calamity. Find answers to your questions and face mysterious creatures along your journey. If war is the closest we get to hell on earth, it’s because Earth harbours the worst of demons: humankind.
Hell is Us will be available August 25 in the US, the UK and Japan.
Umamusume Pretty Derby – Party Dash | PS4
A colorful cast of pixel-art Umamusume are all in line and ready to compete in the Slapdash Grand Prix, a school festival featuring four zany events. Which team will run, shoot, and eat their way to gold and glory? Each team consists of 5 Umamusume, and a total of 4 teams have their eyes on the gold at the Slapdash Grand Prix. The Grand Prix is made up of 4 events: Hurtling Hurdles, Blazing Baskets, Dodgeball Demolition, and Gourmet Gauntlet. Select an Umamusume from your team for each event and aim for the gold, but be prepared for some wacky rules and hijinks!
Umamusume Pretty Derby – Party Dash will be available August 25 in the US, the UK and Japan.
Two Point Museum | PS5
Two Point County’s most daring adventurers have travelled to the far reaches of the known map and returned with unique artefacts to host in your museum, along with the coordinates of a new expedition location, home to an exclusive special exhibit and events! As Curator, the design and management of your expanding museum is in your hands! Send your team of partially trained Experts on Expeditions in search of rare and mostly well-preserved artefacts. When (and hopefully not if) your Experts return from their adventure, proudly display their fantastic finds in your museum.
Two Point Museum will be available August 25 in the US, the UK and Japan.
Metro Exodus | PS5, PS4
Metro Exodus is an epic, story-driven first person shooter from 4A Games that blends deadly combat and stealth with exploration and survival horror. Flee the shattered ruins and embark on an epic, continent-spanning post-apocalyptic journey in the greatest Metro adventure yet. Explore vast, non-linear levels and follow a thrilling story-line inspired by the novels of Dmitry Glukhovsky that spans an entire year through spring, summer and autumn to the depths of nuclear winter.
Metro Exodus will be available August 25 in the US, the UK and Japan.
Dying Light 2 | PS5, PS4
In Dying Light 2, survival meets action adventure as you attempt to endure a hostile, post-apocalyptic world. Rival factions across The City aren’t the only enemy – a virus has turned a vast majority of the human population into monsters. Take on the role of Aiden Caldwell, a wanderer with the power to change the fate of The City, but your exceptional abilities come at a price. Haunted by memories you cannot decipher, you set out to learn the truth – and find yourself in a combat zone. Hone your skills to defeat your enemies and make allies. Unravel the dark secrets behind those that wield power, choose sides and decide your destiny. But wherever your actions take you, there’s one thing you must do – stay human.
Dying Light 2 will be available August 25 in the US, the UK and Japan.
PlayStation Plus Premium
Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams | PS5, PS4
Step back into Feudal Japan and rise as Oni of the Ash — Soki, a strong young warrior, joins forces with his allies to take on powerful demons called Genma. With Oda Nobunaga’s demise, the Genma forces rampaging throughout Japan vanish. Toyotomi Hideyoshi takes control of the land, leading many to believe that peace has returned. On the fateful date of June 29, 1596, a strange planet with a mysterious glow appears in the sky, causing an unexpected change in Hideyoshi. Two years later, as chaos ensues, Hideyoshi embarks on a quest to gather cherry trees from the far reaches of Japan and transport them to the capital. Meanwhile, a young warrior in possession of dark power emerges. Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams originally released on PS2.
Disney’s Atlantis: The Lost Empire | PS5, PS4
Experience Disney’s Atlantis: The Lost Empire first released on the original PlayStation console, now enhanced with up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters. Driven by the legend of Atlantis, join Milo Thatch as he leads a team of experts to unlock the secrets of The Lost Empire. Journey to uncharted depths, far below the ocean surface where hidden dangers swim, lurk and spy from every nook and cranny. What you encounter next will change things forever…
*PlayStation Plus Game Catalog and PlayStation Plus Premium/Deluxe lineups may differ by region. Please check PlayStation Store on release day. Digital PS5 games available to stream from your library will vary over time, region, and country.

title: Kinetic Publishing Showcase recap: 5 new indie games coming to PS5
full_content:
Details on Contact Protocol, Crescent County, Shellbound, Aether Wizard Life, and Precognition.
You may have heard of Kinetic Games through our horror title, Phasmophobia. It’s sold over 27 million copies, and thanks to this success, in January of this year we established our very own publishing label, Kinetic Publishing. Our aim at Kinetic Publishing is to support and empower indie devs to create incredible games, giving them the level of support that our founder, Daniel Knight, would have benefitted from when he was first creating Phasmophobia.
Today we debuted our Kinetic Publishing showcase, where we got to reveal the first five games we’ll be publishing throughout 2027 and 2028. These dev teams all have unique, inspiring stories and just as equally exciting games. From a true sci-fi horror to a witch-tech delivery adventure, and everything in between, we’ve curated a selection of games we hope players are going to love, and of course, they will all be available on PlayStation 5.
Contact Protocol
Can you make the right decisions under pressure? That’s the question the team behind Contact Protocol wants the answer to. In this sci-fi starship job simulator, you are tasked with the scourge that is corporate admin as you assess the intentions of incoming ships on the Pale Horse’s voyage to Jupiter’s largest moon. Compare incoming information against company records and do your best to determine whether ships are friend or foe. But make the wrong decision and all it takes is one torpedo to guarantee your safety – while sending the other crew to their death in the vacuum of space.
In Contact Protocol, players’ cognitive load is gradually ramped up while being offered near-impossible decisions, and we found the combination of this stressful gameplay combined with allocated downtime and the incredible yet somewhat unsettling art style, to be something really special. It’s high stakes, it’s intense, but it’ll leave you coming back for more, as players will soon find out when Contact Protocol launches on PlayStation 5 in Spring 2027.
Crescent County
Crescent County is a game that sings with sunset-soaked, dreamy graphics from the mind of creative director and illustrator, Anna Hollinrake. Based on her own lived experience moving to the Isle of Wight, players will discover what it means to find home on this magical crescent isle. From crunchy, flow-state motorbroom driving, to messy, gossip-fuelled local drama and flirty relationships, Crescent County aims to offer the experience of Kiki’s Delivery Service meets the bikes of Akira set on a rural, witch-tech island.
We couldn’t deny how much we loved the gorgeous, painterly world of Crescent County, a down-to-earth passion project that oozes good vibes. Celebrating queerness, found-family and community in a way we couldn’t ignore, get ready to lose yourself in the beauty of Crescent County when it comes to PlayStation 5 in Summer 2027.
Shellbound
Shellbound has taken the best bits of a metroidvania and set them on a ‘big ass snail’. Giving real meaning to the phrase ‘living world’, players take on the role of a parasite exploring an environment where organs are labyrinths and the snail’s very biology can reshape the paths available to them. The combination of combat and platforming provides the much-loved metroidvania challenge, proving simple to learn but satisfyingly difficult to master.
But Shellbound is pushing the limits of the genre, giving players parasitic powers that allow them to take control of enemies and NPCs and each creature offering unique movement, combat, and traversal skills. Harnessing these abilities is the key to reaching hidden areas, unlocking new routes, and defeating powerful bosses – which players will learn when Shellbound launches on PlayStation 5 in Summer 2028.
Aether Wizard Life
The creativity and ambition of the team at Vonder Games is truly something to behold, as they combine town-building, platforming and exploration with action-RPG combat, farming, and dating in Aether Wizard Life. Players take on the role of an apprentice mage in the haunted town of Starfall, and must uncover the secrets of mysterious wizard kidnappings. Along the way, you are free to choose what tasks to take on each day, whether that’s growing magical crops, caring for exotic creatures, venturing into deep and twisting dungeons to fight monsters, or talking with the townsfolk to discover new side quests and problems to solve.
From the Ghibli-inspired art style, to the story behind the town’s mystery taking inspiration from the fascinating, real history of witches – we were captivated by the team’s attention to detail in Aether Wizard Life. This new cozy wizard life sim launches on Playstation 5 in Autumn 2028.
Precognition
We are beyond excited to announce that we will be partnering with Half Mermaid Productions on their newest game, Precognition. Originally teased under the name ‘Project C’, Precognition is a sci-fi horror being created by Immortality and Her Story creator Sam Barlow in collaboration with acclaimed horror director Brandon Cronenberg. At Kinetic, we’ve played (and gotten hooked on) Sam’s previous FMV games like Immortality and Her Story, and jumped at the chance to work with such a talented team.
Of course, Kinetic is best known for its own horror title, so we’re very happy to have an equally thrilling game in our publishing lineup. And Precognition aims to go one step further than Sam’s previous games, giving players a real sense of agency and freedom in choosing where the story goes. Be sure to interrogate the smallest of details, and get ready to face the consequences that await when you meddle with the flow of time, when Precognition launches on PlayStation 5 in Spring 2028.

title: (For Southeast Asia) Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Comes to PS5 October 2
full_content:
New narrative expansion, new combat survival mode, and much more.
We are so excited to announce that even more new content is coming to Ghost of Yōtei! On October 2, we’ll have a new narrative expansion, new single-player combat survival mode, and new quality of life updates all coming in Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition!1
Before we dive in, we want to take a moment to thank everyone for an incredible year since Ghost of Yōtei launched. We are so proud of our incredible community, and grateful for all of the fan art, cosplays, virtual photographs, combat montages, Twitch streams, Jubei thirst posts…we promise we’ve seen it all and love to share it around the studio. Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition will launch just in time for our 1-year anniversary, and we can’t wait for another year of new creations from all of you!
In the coming weeks we’ll have much more to share, but wanted to give you a few early looks today at the new content in Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition:
Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara is our new narrative expansion. Split between the present day and flashbacks to Atsu’s time on the mainland, you’ll meet Nagato, a figure from Atsu’s past who has arrived in Ezo. In the present, you’ll explore a previously unseen valley once inhabited by The Snake and his gang of loyal followers, the Vipers. In the past, you’ll experience Atsu’s time in the Battle of Sekigahara and a key moment in her life before she returned home for her quest for vengeance. You’ll meet new enemies and find new heavy weapons, new armor sets, new dyes, and more.
Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted is a brand new single-player combat survival mode, our spin on a roguelike. You’ll accept bounties in order to start new runs, where taking down enemies will earn you perks, as well as unlock additional characters to play as. We’ll have much more to show soon, but as you can see in the trailer today, Atsu is a master with the dual katana, while Oyuki excels with the kusarigama, and Nagato shines with a yari. We love to watch the amazing combat reels that have been shared with us on social media, and can’t wait to see you all try to perfect these runs.
If you haven’t experienced Atsu’s journey yet, you can purchase Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition for SGD 89.90 (Disc Version) / SGD 97.90 (Digital Version) / MYR 299 (Disc/Digital Version) / IDR 1,169,000 (Disc Version) / IDR 1,142,000 (Digital Version) / THB 2,290 (Disc/Digital Version) / PHP 4,099 (Disc Version) / VND 1,799,000 (Disc Version). In addition to Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted, this includes the award-winning main Ghost of Yōtei game as well as Ghost of Yōtei Legends, our online co-op experience with support for up to four players and multiple gameplay modes culminating in a Raid.2 If you purchase the Complete Edition, you can immediately start playing the main game and Legends, and Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted will arrive with a patch on October 2.
Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition also includes all of the in-game content previously included in the Ghost of Yōtei Digital Deluxe Edition, as well as the Charm of Hokkyokusei. If you purchase by September 30, you’ll also get an early unlock of the Sakai Armor on October 2 for Atsu to wear, a throwback to Jin’s family armor from Ghost of Tsushima.1
If you already own Ghost of Yōtei, you can get Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted by purchasing the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition Upgrade (Digital Only) for SGD 20.27 / MYR 60.11 / IDR 220,890 / THB 524 If you don’t already own the Digital Deluxe Edition and Charm of Hokkyokusei you’ll immediately unlock that content upon pre-ordering. And if you pre-order by September 30, on October 2 you’ll also get the early unlock of the Sakai Armor.
Beyond the new content listed above, Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition includes new tracks for Watanabe Mode that will be available throughout the entire game when the mode is enabled. There’s also new photo mode stamps, additional cosmetics for New Game+, and new Trophies for both Echoes of Sekigahara and Most Wanted.
For anyone who owns Ghost of Yōtei, even without purchasing the Complete Edition upgrade, a new patch on October 2 will add the new Beauty of Yōtei mode, which allows for a screensaver-like view of the environments of Ezo to keep on and relax at home (and take stunning new Photo Mode captures). There will also be new quality of life features including the option to keep an armor set’s appearance while using a different set’s stats, as well as a new high contrast accessibility option.1
Thank you again to everyone for an amazing year since Ghost of Yōtei launched! We’ll have more to share about Most Wanted and Echoes of Sekigahara as we get closer to launch on October 2, so be sure to follow our social media channels and keep an eye out!
1 Available via patch v.2.0 on October 1, 2026 globally, and October 2, 2026 in some territories, including Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. Internet connection and account for PlayStation required to download.
2 Online multiplayer requires a PlayStation Plus subscription. PS Plus is subject to a recurring subscription fee taken automatically until cancellation. Full terms: play.st/psplus-usageterms.

title: Hands-on report: Marvel’s Wolverine
full_content:
Logan teams up with Mystique and Sabretooth to take on the anti-mutant billionaire Trask.
It’s been a big week for fans of Marvel’s Wolverine, starting with the announcement of sharp-looking PS5 hardware and accessories. Now, with just over a month away until its September 15 launch, Insomniac is sharing a deep dive on the game’s story, combat, and exploration thanks to an extensive hands-on session with the game.
Our two-hour session kicked off with the game’s opening mission in the wilds of Telambang, where Wolverine has reunited with Team X to carry out a critical mission infiltrating the facility of anti-mutant industrialist Bolivar Trask. After slicing our way to a daring rescue, we jumped ahead in the game to a bombastic boss fight and a taste of Madripoor’s Lowtown. Between brutal barrages, stealthy scouting, and a range of rage-filled takedowns, we got to cut to the bone of the game’s story, flesh out Wolverine’s allies and foes, and uncover a piece of his buried past.
Taking on Trask
From the game’s opening moments flashing back to a feral, mangy-haired, and memory-wiped Wolverine, every sequence tested the balance between his rage and humanity. The first mission reunites him with Team X, a mutant task force formed by Nathaniel Essex to help protect mutants. Wolverine had stepped away from the group, something that has rankled his teammates, a wry Mystique and ever-savage Sabretooth.
Their mission takes them from the hidden facility of billionaire Bolivar Trask to the seedy backstreets of Madripoor, presenting Wolverine with the grim reality of what mutants in this world are facing. With mutants largely unknown by society, Trask has been spending his billions abducting, studying, and cruelly disposing of mutants with little regard for his victims in a quest to maintain human superiority. As the nefarious reality of the facility’s purpose becomes clearer, the horror Wolverine feels quickly pools into an unbridled rage. That rage drives him forward through throngs of Reaver enemies and a run in with Omega Red to eventually free Essex, who has been held captive by Trask.
Essex is the one who found Wolverine years before in that feral state, and formed Team X to protect mutants and build a world where mutants can be open. Between Essex and Trask, Wolverine is faced with the lengths some will go to protect the future of their kind, and will challenge him to face what kind of person he wants to be in this future.
Sink your claws in
Between storylines and set pieces, my biggest takeaway from my time with Marvel’s Wolverine was that it feels dang good to sink those claws in. Wolverine doesn’t just attack enemies, he catapults himself at them, targeting and launching himself from across the room to stun or barrage. Every combat encounter becomes a furious flurry, where my adrenaline feels directly tied to Wolverine’s increasing rage.
While a simple parry and barrage can get the job done, Wolverine can unlock a number of Special Techniques, skills that can be upgraded and mapped to the directional buttons for an extra flair in a fight. In my playthrough, I could cleave through a group surrounding me with Tornado Spin, or interrupt enemy attacks with Knee Breaker. Players can also unlock Adaptations, which upgrade long-term effects and skills like Logan’s health and rage meter.
That rage will come in handy. Successful combos build up Wolverine’s rage meter, which rises through three Rage Tiers to dramatically alter his fighting style. As Wolverine enters Rage Tier 2, his combos become more powerful and he unlocks Last Stand, which allows him to use his rage to heal his body if fully downed. But things really go over the edge when Wolverine’s meter fills to Rage Tier 3. His attacks become significantly more powerful, while brutal critical strikes become available. His vision seems to close in, his breathing getting louder and more primal as he darts between enemies, slicing and dicing with ease. Those critical strikes can lead to some dangerously fun takedowns, like snatching a member of The Hand’s katana or bow to slam back into them.
Sometimes, Wolverine needs a more methodical approach. He can use his Enhanced Senses to track and takedown enemies more stealthily. Trask also has Ability Inhibitors at his disposal that block Wolverine and his teammates from using their abilities. In these moments, he must work past the pain and fight without healing, focusing on taking enemies down with classic combat moves and destroying the Inhibitors before it’s too late.
It took all the skills I had gathered so far to take on the looming Sentinel Prototype towards the end of my preview. Built by Trask to detect and destroy mutants, this fight took all of Wolverine’s patience and strategy, dodging or parrying the Sentinel’s powerful attacks, while waiting for the perfect moments to strike. This sequence was thrilling both to use Wolverine’s abilities to their fullest potential, and to watch as he worked in tandem with Mystique and Sabretooth. By the time I was busting through the Sentinel’s head victorious, I had a wild grin on my face and felt amped and ready to take on anyone.
More to explore
Luckily after that fight, there was still more to explore. In Madripoor, surrounded by allies new and old, we took a moment of respite in Princess Bar (run by Tyger). Here we got to interact with newly acquired ally Jean Grey, and the mutant teens she has been protecting. Though they are still a mystery to one another, Jean and Wolverine’s connection is immediate. It’s with her that he can admit that his anger sometimes scares him and that he wants to be better.
I enjoyed that Wolverine also makes time here for his teammates Mystique and Sabretooth. Mystique stays focused and on mission during combat, shifting through identities when needed. Here in Princess Bar, she can just be herself, and encourages Wolverine to do the same through a friendly but vulnerable game of Never Have I Ever. Sabretooth spends most of the game’s opening antagonizing Wolverine and calling him a runt, which is fair enough given he stands about as tall as Sabretooth’s navel. But it’s clear their relationship runs deeper, and Sabretooth feels spurned by Wolverine’s original exit from the group.
While exploring the streets of Lowtown, I could take the time to check out some of Wolverine’s other looks and claw types, which ranged from a classic undershirt and jeans outfit to a Weapon X helmeted style. While walking around the Princess Bar, Wolverine’s Enhanced Senses could pick up on conversation or music that could guide him to specific rooms, or trail a teammate’s scent to find where they’ve run off to. Exploring each room sometimes led to a conversation, or finding easter eggs, like Mystique’s wedding pictures, or an IOU written on an ace of spades card from one Remy LeBeau.
Take the time to explore each new location, as Wolverine can discover hidden crates with raw upgrade materials or collectable whisky bottles. Logan can also stumble across Nightmare Doors, which transport him to a dreamlike cabin to take part in a Nightmare Trial. These timed speed trials reimagine different locations from the game into a vertical fever dream, where he can race to the end to unlock a forgotten memory from his past.
Players can sink their claws into Wolverine’s story and tap into his rage when Marvel’s Wolverine launches September 15 on PS5 consoles.

title: New It Happens on PS5 campaign highlights the biggest moments of play
full_content:
The ad debuts this week with special installations and local activations bringing PS5 moments to life around the world.
There’s never been a better time to play on PS5. With a lineup of iconic games available now and coming soon, players have plenty of unforgettable experiences to look forward to. From new stories featuring legendary Marvel characters in Marvel’s Wolverine as well as 007 First Light, and God of War Laufey, to the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI, the most-exciting adventures ahead will happen on PS5.
Today, we’re launching a new It Happens on PS5 hero advert highlighting what’s available on PS5 as well as what’s ahead for players in the coming months. The advert invites players to discover what PS5 makes possible, taking viewers on a fast-paced journey through bold and unexpected moments, featuring larger-than-life scenes, from Giannis Antetokounmpo’s elite basketball skills that get the streets bouncing to a high-speed jet ski chase.
Across the world, It Happens on PS5 comes to life beyond the screen through creators, special installations, and activations. With Marvel’s Wolverine launching on September 15, players may encounter game-inspired experiences, including Marvel’s Wolverine challenge pods in France and a Berserker Mode activation in Australia. Players in the UK, Canada, and Spain may also find larger-than-life Sentinel head installations, with other locations celebrating memorable moments from fan-favorite PS5 games.
We look forward to seeing what players discover next and celebrate play on PS5.

full_content:
Disney also shared some news about its ever-expanding life-sim adventure Disney Dreamlight Valley at D23 this week.
Following the recently released Honeyglow Woods Adventure Pack and the latest free update Pixel Perfect, fans have now been given a first-look at the game's fourth expansion, The Keepsake Sea. It includes a teaser of Jack Sparrow and will be "coming soon".
The same panel also provided some additional news, detailing several major updates on the way (including the Hannah Montana & Lizzie McGuire collection, arriving on 19th August 2026).
Here's what you can expect (via the PR), and you can check out the trailers above and below:
- An exclusive first look at Disney Dreamlight Valley: The Keepsake Sea
  - The official title and first details of the game's fourth Expansion were shared.
  - An exclusive teaser trailer offered a preview of the exciting adventure awaiting players later this year.
- Oogie Boogie takes over the Valley this Halloween
  - A scary new Villager will make his debut in Disney Dreamlight Valley. Oogie Boogie from Disney Tim Burton’s The Nightmare Before Christmas will make his debut as part of a brand-new Halloween event, bringing frightfully fun surprises to the Valley.
  - In the lead-up to Halloween, players can also look forward to weekly quests, themed rewards, and seasonal festivities.
- Lilo joins the Valley this holiday season
  - The final free update of the year will welcome Lilo from Disney's Lilo & Stitch, allowing players to finally experience her long-awaited reunion with Stitch.
- Hannah Montana & Lizzie McGuire collection arrives August 19
  - A brand-new Premium Shop collection inspired by Hannah Montana and Lizzie McGuire launches next week, giving players the chance to style their Avatars in a few superstar-inspired outfits.
You can rewatch the entire Disney Dreamlight Valley D23 panel on the game's official YouTube channel.

title: Talking Point: Is An Analogue 3D Worth The Money?
full_content:
GoldenTry 007
I've wanted one since it was first announced back in 2023, of course. Just as an object, the Analogue 3D is a handsome re-imagining of the original's Romanesque stylings, a form I called "stately yet sensual" in a piece I wrote for The Console Chronicles a while back. Analogue removed the 'pillars' on either side but captured the curves and that smooth hump across the front, just with a smaller footprint. Add in the light-up controller ports and it's a slick bit of kit.
Expensive, too. Right now it's listed on Analogue's website for $269.99 plus shipping. As a 'luxury' way to play games I can already play in multiple ways, it was high on desires but low on my priority list. Add in import charges and this economy, and no, I'd make do with NSO and OG hardware with an EON Super 64.
So what pushed me over the edge? Ultimately, two things:
- Actually playing one at a Hookshot staff meetup in May (nothing like the ego boost of winning a couple of rounds of GoldenEye to fuel a frivolous purchase, but feeling and seeing how it performed firsthand convinced me it was legit)
- The ballooning prices of just about everything video-game related right now (ie. it definitely ain't gonna get cheaper)
Another factor was that, as noted above, the N64 is my childhood console. Having seen the Analogue NT come and go and shoot up to insane money secondhand, was I going to let this slip through my fingers only to pay twice as much for one in five years’ time?
Armed with those watertight justifications, I took to the internet on payday to hunt down a deal.
Living in Europe, unpredictable tariffs and crazy import/shipping fees made me wary of buying direct from the US. I've been stung by import charges on my doorstep before and I just didn't want that uncertainty. (Seriously, having to pay a driver with actual cash — not card — feels like a scam in 2026, but hey, that's another article.)
eBay had various listings for sealed systems, particularly the white one, which, if the reaction of my NL colleagues is a barometer of public sentiment, isn't the one people want — especially not after Analogue released all those limited 'Funtastic' variants. It was, however, the one that I wanted. This was going to stay hooked up permanently in the living room, and the unassuming pale one would sit on the TV stand very nicely alongside my Wii and PS5 (my Switch 2 is docked around the back).
I have Nintendo's NSO controller plus a bunch of originals, so I didn't need a pad. However, the listing I found bundled a white 8BitDo 64, and another wireless pad which plays nicely with N64 games is handy.
Satisfied in the knowledge that there were no 'hidden' import charges or taxes involved — and no international shipping wait times — I put in the minimum bid, won, and two days later I had the thing on my desk.
All-in, this thing is a significant retro investment; it set me back €370 with the controller. At the time of writing, a Switch 2 costs just €100 more.
First impressions
Analogue has a knack for design and presentation, and that starts right from the packaging, with a soft-feel black box that looks the part before you've even opened it. Likewise, the white SD card in the box is a bespoke affair with the Analogue logo cut into it, with the colour-matched cables similarly branded.
Making the controller an add-on is a sticking point for some, although for me the lack of an EU-friendly USB-C power adapter was a minor issue. No dice with a Mac or an iPhone charger, so right now I'm using my Switch 2 plug - which is fine, but it means switching cables when I switch consoles.
Updating firmware via the SD card was straightforward, and I like how the light on the front is also a sync button - and how the controller ports light up sequentially as a 'progress bar' during updates. I'd prefer a printed instruction sheet to a QR code, but that's just me, and before long I had the latest firmware with save states (or 'Memories' as Analogue dubbed them) and was ready to rock.
The OS is clean and clear, and you can tailor your display preferences for each individual game easily enough. It's not as granular as you'll find on some upscaling solutions, but there's more than enough tweaks to be made if you know your PVMs from your BVMs, or just want something authentic-looking on your modern 4K display.
I've found myself defaulting to BVM (Broadcast Video Monitor) for most games with the Integer+ fill option. I want it to look like it was designed to on a CRT, so scanlines and some softening are a must, and tweaking on a per-game basis is handy.
The recently-added horizontal upscaling option produces great results when I turned it on for Episode 1 Racer — again, check out My Life in Gaming's recent video which explores the 1.5.0 update. For someone who finds Nintendo Switch Online's CRT filter a passable display option (it's incorrect aspect ratios that really wind me up), the Analogue 3D covers all my bases and then some.
On the topic of NSO, as convenient as it is, going back will be tough once you've sampled this. Beginning an Ocarina playthrough recently (did you hear they're remaking it?), I changed to NSO when I realised I'd want to play it with the kids on a summer break and Switch 2 is easier to sling in a suitcase. But even with a game that doesn't require lightning reflexes, the input latency was startling by comparison.
I noticed it most when playing the Ocarina itself - the gap between hitting a C-button and hearing the note felt enormous on Switch 2 and it made a couple of sections noticeably harder; specifically, copying the frog chorus in Zora's River and the battle against Dark Link.
The lag wasn't a dealbreaker — not when you've got the rewind feature to fall back on — but ignorance really is bliss. So, know that you'll spoil yourself for any lesser option once you've played Zelda's Lullaby on the A3D.
And OoT isn't even something that depends on twitch reflexes. Games like F-Zero X, Wave Race 64, and 1080 feel soupy on Switch at the best of times; the Analogue transforms them back into the immediate, responsive racers they are/were. GoldenEye feels snappy once more.
I won't just list titles here, but spending significant time with games like Rogue Squadron and Snowboard Kids has been a joy in the last few weeks. I've got family coming to visit soon, and I've already got an old-school multiplayer session programmed in.
My odd curiosity to one day play Quest 64 will soon be satisfied, too - that is if I can stop playing the aforementioned Episode 1: Racer. The elegance of that game's controls coupled with the speed (and, undeniably, a good shot of nostalgia) is just beautiful - check out Jack's recent Making Of interview with the devs over on Time Extension if you're an avid podracer. Fingers crossed for a Switch 2 port of Galactic Racer.

title: ARK: Survival Evolved Sunsets Official Switch Servers This Month
full_content:
Developer Studio Wildcard has announced official server support for the Switch version of its dinosaur-themed survival game Ark: Survival Evolved will be sunset at the end of August.
The studio shared this news in a community update on the game's message boards. This will also apply to ARK: Ultimate Survivor Edition, a "rebuilt Switch remaster" by Grove Street Games released in 2022.
Here's the official announcement about the official server shutdown for this platform:
Ark Nintendo Switch Announcement
It is with wistful hearts that today we are announcing the Official Servers for 'ARK: Survival Evolved and ARK: Ultimate Survivor Edition' on Nintendo Switch will sunset on August 31st, 2026. Over a million players have explored these servers since the original ARK Switch release in 2018 and the launch of Grove Street Games' rebuilt Switch remaster in 2022. We want to thank everyone who has been a part of this journey.
Please note that Unofficial Servers and Single Player modes will continue to remain fully playable after this date.
As noted, unofficial servers and single-player will remain "fully playable" beyond this date. You can find out more about this game and the updated version in our previous coverage:

full_content:
Update []: During the D23 Kingdom Hearts "Deep Dive" panel, Disney and Square Enix shared an extended Coco trailer for Kingdom Hearts IV. It shows the world of Coco, Mickey's paper universe, and there are gameplay segments featuring Mickey, Donald, and Goofy.
Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue has also reiterated the game will be arriving in 2027, and development has been "very smooth" so far:
"At this year's D23 we were finally able to announce a release date for Kingdom Hearts IV, I'm really excited about that as well, and I can confidently say and promise that it will launch in 2027. And yeah, so schedule-wise, development is very smooth. It's not like an 80% thing, 90% thing, it's a 100% thing, so we'll be there for sure. So, promise you that."
Creative director Tetsuya Nomura added to this, stating he's aware of fan speculation about delays and says this won't be happening:
"We announced the game is going to be coming late 2027, and I saw online some people were saying the actual release date might still get pushed back. I just wanted to set the record straight that is not happening."
Original Story: [Sat 15th Aug, 2026 04:55 BST]:
At Disney's D23 event this week, Kingdom Hearts fans got another look at Kingdom Hearts IV in a new showcase trailer.
The end of the trailer also confirms the anticipated title will be launching on all platforms, including the Switch 2, in "late 2027". Here's the official announcement, which also mentions how Pixar's Coco will feature in Sora's new adventure.
"Revealed during the Disney Entertainment Showcase on August 14, 2026, KINGDOM HEARTS IV is launching in late 2027! A brand-new adventure awaits as the world of Disney and Pixar's Coco joins KINGDOM HEARTS IV."
In some related news, Disney has also announced a Kingdom Hearts anime series is "coming soon" to Disney+ and the Disney Channel.
"Ready for a new adventure? An original Kingdom Hearts anime series inspired by the beloved video game franchise is coming soon to Disney Channel and Disney+"

title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta Adds Campaign Mission 'Entrenched'
full_content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is getting an open beta at the end of this month, and all platforms (including Switch 2) are invited.
Activision and Infinity Ward have now provided an update, announcing the beta will also allow players to experience a campaign mission. Players will have access to the "Entrenched" mission, which can be seen in the "first look" trailer above.
The open beta will get underway on 28th August 2026 and runs until 1st September 2026. This will apparently be the first time a Call of Duty beta has given players access to a campaign mission.
So, you'll be able to not only get a feel for how the multiplayer experience is, but also see how the blockbuster single-player experience holds up on Nintendo's new hybrid system.
Activision will also be hosting an "Early Access" beta, but as you can see in the graphic above, Switch 2 users are not included in this. You can find out more details about this upcoming beta in our previous coverage.
More "first look" Call of Duty campaign mission trailers can be viewed on the official Call of Duty YouTube page.

title: Mailbox: Zelda-Themed Switch 2s, Kiddy Consoles, "Take My Money, Nintendo" Scenarios - Nintendo Life Letters
full_content:
Welcome to the August 2026 edition of the Nintendo Life Mailbox.
It's been a particularly hot summer around these parts. The moon did its best to block out the sun last week and give us some respite from the heat, but we've still sitting around Nintendo Life Towers in various states of (HR-compliant) undress, surrounded by fans and iced beverages. Hopefully you're keeping cool wherever you are!
Now it's time for our monthly letters page feature. Got something you want to get off your chest? We're ready and waiting to read about your game-related ponderings.
Each month we’ll highlight a Star Letter, the writer of which will receive a month’s subscription to our ad-free Supporter scheme. Check out the submission guidelines at the bottom of this page.
Let's sit back with cool drink and go through our dispatch box, shall we? No hot takes this month, please.
Nintendo Life Mailbox - August 2026
"buffet of our deepest desires" (***STAR LETTER***)
I have been saying for the last decade or so, if Nintendo remake either The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time or Super Mario 64 in glorious HD, I would throw £100 at either game, no questions asked.
So I'm pretty stoked that OOT is finally getting the HD treatment and then some, and who knows, it may even retail for half the amount I'm happy to pay.
It's always been a "Take my money Nintendo" scenario; it's a little crazy it took this long but if one game deserves to be repainted and brushed up for modern audiences, it's Ocarina - a true landmark in the medium.
While I'm happy if it's a 1-2-1 remake, I can't help but feel Nintendo are up to something more. Why tease so little mere months away from release? Why stop short of showing Hyrule field or even a dungeon?
It could be one of two scenarios: trolling us, or hiding something from us. Hopefully, Hyrule Field will be expanded and made into a mini breath of the wild esque open world with way more to do than before.
If so, then I am excited for the future of Zelda. Because as great as the Botw and Totk era was, I think most Zelda nuts like me miss a good, honest dungeon.
So the OOT remake presents an opportunity for Nintendo to dip their toes into combining the best of the new with the old. They could even, if they wanted, retool the dungeons a little ala Master Quest version of OOT.
Of course, I may be wrong. If Nintendo can bring back the Virtual Boy in 2026, they can troll with the best and tease us "just cos".
But either way, wrong or not, Nintendo will rediscover what makes a great Zelda dungeon by remaking OOT, and hopefully the next Zelda, will give us the full dungeon and open world buffet of our deepest desires and be the GOOAT (Greatest Ocarina of All Time)...
YoshiTails
Re. Nintendo not revealing much yet, the moment you properly show off the Ocarina remake, it'll suck up all the air and discourse in the room. From a bland marketing perspective, if you're plugging a game like Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave over the summer (a very different game, granted, but still a fantasy swords-and-tunics affair to the layplayer), you're better off waiting until that's gone through its pre-release cycle before dropping an Ocarina Direct. I wouldn't expect new news (beyond leaks) until September.
I'd love it if Aonuma and Fujibayashi and the EPD Zelda team had been working on this since TOTK wrapped up — I'd far prefer a serious overhaul than a delicate 1:1 remake, personally — but I'd temper expectations if you're hoping for open-world Ocarina. The timing of this feels complementary to next April's movie, and Nintendo will want to have the next instalment lined up for 2028/29. As I wrote last week, my money's on a Grezzo special. Not long to find out, though. - Ed.
