title: How student athletes are changing the game
full_content:
The program’s participants, pictured on their first day at Red Hat
On June 1, the first cohort of student athletes arrived at the Raleigh office to take part in the Red Hat Sales Combine Accelerator Program. The group of 6 engaged in a newly launched 3-week micro-internship, using skills carefully honed on the playing field and translating them into the world of technology sales.
The pilot program at Red Hat is the first of its kind, aimed at collaboration with emerging talent who possess unique skills and insight. In addition to their position as students, the participants balance their role as athletes, and navigate those commitments through the summer. The internship was crafted with flexibility, taking their training schedules into consideration. We spoke to some of the program participants and mentors to learn more about how an athletic career translates to a role in the technology industry, and about their experiences in the pilot program.
Rory Jones Amen Hetep, a rising senior and wide receiver at North Carolina A&T State University, cited discipline when asked how his sport has shaped him as an individual today.
“Obviously, I love football, but I don't want to wake up at 5 AM every day,” said Rory. “But, just knowing that I have to do something for a higher goal, I take that way beyond the football field.”
Rory also mentioned collaboration as a foundational trait he learned from football, with the sport teaching him about connecting with different people who are all aligned towards a single goal.
As a result of those grueling 5 AM workouts, fast-paced practices, and packed weeks, the group holds an unparalleled set of skills. Being committed, driven, and coachable are synonymous with their identities as student athletes. But what really changes the game—transforming a competitive match-up into a momentous win—is the thread of connection between teammates. That spirit of connection and community was apparent as the student athletes made their mark at the Raleigh office.
“You know, on the field, when you're first bonding with teammates, there's a lot of disconnection,” said Rory. “You’re not sure how you're the same, you're not sure how to connect, and that was sort of the same in the corporate space.”
Rory explained that he took advantage of being in the office—taking the time to learn about his fellow interns and experiencing Red Hatters beyond the internship program and the office setting.
“I've made some really good friends here in just 3 weeks that I will probably remember for a really long time,” he reflected. “So, there's a lot of similarities between having a teammate and having a coworker, and I’ve been able to take advantage of both.”
The student athletes spent their days immersed in the world of technology sales, researching Red Hat sales strategy to generate potential areas of improvement. In addition to daily meetings, check-ins with mentors, and collaboration with other interns, the cohort was invited to several workshops on various topics, including personal branding and professional development. Social mixers—including a “Rep Your School” event—provided a space for the interns to learn from fellow Red Hatters, ask questions, and share their own unique experiences.
The participants also had the opportunity to connect with former athletes at Red Hat, learning the ways their repertoire of skills might be molded to increase their impact in the workplace.
One of those former athletes was Joy Wilkerson, a public relations specialist at Red Hat and former collegiate basketball player. Joy shared some reflections about her personal journey and the ways relationships formed on a team translate in the office.
“While the connections forged on the field are born from the raw accountability of shared physical suffering, they translate into the workplace as high-level emotional intelligence, tactical collaboration, and a unique immunity to taking constructive criticism personally.”
“Ultimately, ex-athletes bridge the gap between these 2 worlds by treating corporate projects like high-stakes games—they know how to adapt to different roles, build psychological safety within a group, and rally a professional team to execute a vision when the pressure is on.”
The internship ended with a capstone presentation where participants presented findings from their research
Morgan Salzano, HR business partner, agrees that some of the habits formed during her college softball career show up in her professional life, sometimes in unexpected ways.
“I had a meeting recently that I really wanted to go well, and I found myself slipping right back into my old pregame routine: a good breakfast, music that put me in the right headspace, and plenty of positive self-talk.
I noticed that I felt the same adrenaline I used to feel before stepping into the circle to pitch a softball game, except now I’m preparing for moments that stretch me professionally, instead of games on a field.”
The 3-week micro internship culminated in a final presentation during which the student athletes presented their findings to an open audience, including members of the sales team and their fellow interns. Delivered either in pairs or individually, all the presentations involved strategic analysis of the sales team. Some presenters opted to take on the role of prospective clients, analyzing Red Hat’s technology as opposed to its competitors. All of the presenters offered insight on forward-thinking improvements.
At the program’s conclusion, Jenna Skibbe, a lacrosse player at Davidson College, told us that the biggest highlight was evaluating a real business challenge.
“It’s a great opportunity to gain exposure to the tech industry, apply skills I've developed as a student-athlete, and connect with other students and professionals,” expressed Jenna. “I’m thankful for the experience and everything I learned throughout the program.”
Overall, the program is a valuable reminder of the mutual learning and innovation potential gained from collaboration with emerging talent from varied backgrounds and experiences. Senior Program Manager, Amy Hedgepeth, who led the rollout of the pilot program and provided the student athletes with the resources to hone their skills and create meaningful impact during their time at Red Hat, commented on the future of the program after the final presentations.
“The student athlete micro-internship proved to be a resounding success, both in terms of participant and mentor feedback,” shared Amy. “Scaling or extending this initiative represents a premier opportunity to connect with competitive future talent, and we look forward to hosting future cohorts of this program."
Want to stay connected about upcoming Emerging Talent programs at Red Hat? Keep an eye on our careers site and sign up for our Talent Community to get updates on future opportunities.

title: ODC-Noord: Building blocks for an existing government cloud
full_content:
How did a small team in the east of the Netherlands (Groningen) from the Government Datacenter North (ODC-Noord) grow into a supplier of crucial building blocks for the Netherlands digital government strategy? Jaap Jansma, Manager of ODC-Noord, and Marcel Timmer, Country Director Netherlands at Red Hat, explain.
ODC-Noord implements, manages, and operates as a scalable, sovereign cloud service for the Dutch government, and Red Hat provides the fundamental open source software. Together, the 2 companies look at what’s needed to continue fulfilling this role within the government, ranging from scalability and digital sovereignty to security-rich AI development within the central government.
ODC-Noord was established in 2012 as part of the Compacte Rijksdienst (Compact Central Government) program, which aimed to reduce the number of central government datacenters from 65 to 4. In Groningen, a small team saw an opportunity to do this both more efficiently and in a way that prepares ODC-Noord for the future. Today, the result is much more than a technical platform. ODC-Noord forms an important foundation for the digital government and, consequently, public service delivery.
“At the time, we received a request from the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Science (OCW) asking if we could deliver a platform for their application landscape,” says Jansma. “That was the moment to build a platform based on open source that we could offer not only to OCW, but also to other parties within the central government.”
In 2016, ODC-Noord's community cloud went live as a standardized Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) platform. A container platform based on Red Hat OpenShift followed in 2018. Today, ODC-Noord serves 48 different organizations across 11 ministries in the Netherlands.
Generic services: Less customization, more efficiency
ODC-Noord delivers generic, scalable, and standardized services, thereby contributing to an efficient government, says Jansma. “We want to move away from unnecessary customization and duplicate work. By having multiple parties use the same solution, we create economies of scale. As a result, one of our core rates has been more than halved.”
This approach also affects the way collaboration happens within central government IT. ODC-Noord delivers efficient platform services, but customers need more, such as digital workspaces, application development, and functional management. “You can be complementary within the government there and actively seek out collaboration,” says Jansma. “We want to prevent the same thing from being built multiple times across different datacenters.”
ODC-Noord started as a greenfield, without legacy systems or personnel. This provided room for an innovative start. But the question remains: How do you retain that innovative power and stay attractive in a tight labor market?
        You have to give tech experts substantive freedom and room to work on what they find important. At the same time, that requires awareness. It has to be secure, financially viable, and within government frameworks. That mix of autonomy and responsibility works well for us.
For many IT professionals, purpose is weighing increasingly heavily, Timmer notes. “It's special to be able to say that you're contributing to one of the building blocks of a sovereign cloud for the government. You're not working on yet another consumer app, but on infrastructure that affects a large part of the public sector.”
A sovereign cloud on an open source foundation
Digital sovereignty is a central theme in the public sector. From the start, ODC-Noord chose open source as its strategic foundation. The infrastructure runs on Dutch soil under the responsibility of civil servants. This intentionally addresses a major part of the sovereignty puzzle.
“We strive for the highest possible degree of digital sovereignty,” says Jansma. “By deploying open source, hosting in the Netherlands, and working with our own people, we maintain control.” The platform complies with relevant security standards and BIO frameworks. The BIO (Baseline Informatiebeveiliging Overheid) is the mandatory information security standard for all government organizations. A new BIO 2 certification is currently in its final stages.
“Dependencies will always exist,” says Timmer. “However, with open source the control remains entirely in your hands. You are never locked in. Even without Red Hat, you can continue using the software, giving the government true technological independence. Sovereignty is whether you have control over your software and hardware. Can you, if worst comes to worst, migrate to another environment within a limited timeframe? That is the benchmark we are setting with ODC-Noord.”
Planning for security-first AI within the National Digitalization Strategy
Alongside an IaaS platform for virtual machines (VMs)—enabling multiple operating systems to run on a single physical server—and a container platform, ODC-Noord is working on the next logical step: an AI platform tailored to the needs of the central government. Demand from clients is growing rapidly.
“On one hand, we host enterprise applications on our VM platform; on the other, modern, cloud-native apps on containers,” says Jansma. “On top of that, a clear need is now emerging for an AI development platform. This must be secure, manageable, and fit within the frameworks of the central government, our National Digitalization Strategy [NDS], and the [Artificial Intelligence Act EU].”
AI requires different building blocks than traditional workloads. “For AI, you need accelerators, GPUs [graphics processing units], and LLMs [large language models],” Timmer explains. “With this shared platform, it fundamentally doesn't matter which GPUs or LLMs you want to use. What matters more is having control, transparency, and clear guardrails within a private environment. This allows government organizations to experiment and scale up with AI faster and more securely.”
The foundation—the "toolbox," as Jansma calls it—lies in the infrastructure ODC-Noord has already built: a modern, open source configuration where AI services can land in a controlled manner.
Growth limits and scarce resources
In practice, ambitions surrounding AI run into physical limitations. “Just like everyone else, we are facing hardware shortages,” Jansma points out. “Can we secure the GPUs we need? And how do we deal with the energy network congestion?” In parts of the Netherlands, datacenters compete with other societal needs—such as households wishing to connect home batteries—for capacity on the electricity grid.
"It would be beneficial if the status of datacenters as infrastructure kept pace with the government's digital ambitions," says Timmer. "That is an issue requiring further coordination."
“Furthermore, it is difficult to determine exactly how much capacity will be needed in advance. We have to discover a lot of this through trial and error,” Jansma adds. “A client procures a platform from us and deploys a model. Only then do you see how much capacity it actually demands. This is precisely why it makes sense to concentrate scarce resources. Not every government organization needs to purchase and manage its own GPU clusters. By investing jointly in a shared foundation, more parties can benefit, and waste is prevented.”
National Digitalization Strategy: Build on what you have
Within the digitalization strategy, the cloud priority revolves around a coherent cloud strategy for the central government. Jansma sees a clear role for ODC-Noord here. “What the NDS aims to achieve, we can already deliver to a large extent. We have an IaaS layer and a container platform. At its core, that is a very strong proposition for a sovereign cloud for the government.”
Timmer observes the same pattern. “There are countless initiatives in the Netherlands. It's good that they exist, but people should look in their own backyard first. A large portion of what you want to have in the long run is already running at ODC-Noord. Use those existing investments and ways of working as a springboard.”
The core message: A sovereign cloud for the government already exists
Both Jansma and Timmer emphasize that the public sector often underestimates what’s already available.
“It would be great if people better understood that a form of cloud already exists within the [Dutch] government,” says Jansma. “A cloud that is highly sovereign, possesses significant innovative power, and is already being utilized by dozens of organizations.”
Timmer summarizes: “There is already a sovereign cloud for the [Dutch] government. Collaborate—both within the government and with the market—and make use of what is already there. ODC-Noord is a front-runner in this regard, with a number of building blocks already in place. It is a waste to keep starting over from scratch.”

title: How we built an AI agent for field associates with Red Hat AI
full_content:
Sellers need information in order to do their jobs. At most organizations, this information already exists in various internal systems. The challenge facing every sales team isn't finding that information; it's turning it into action fast enough to matter.
To address this challenge, we built Sales Assistant, an enterprise AI agent powered by Red Hat AI and used by Red Hat sellers internally. Sales Assistant surfaces appropriate context, takes action, completes tasks, streamlines workflows, and frees sellers to focus on customers.
For Red Hat sellers, critical data lives across Salesforce, product documentation, pricing systems, lifecycle databases, and internal knowledge bases. Each system serves an important purpose, but together they can create fragmented workflows. Preparing for customer conversations often means switching between multiple applications to gather context, validate information, and complete routine tasks.
Red Hat sellers didn’t lack data or tooling—but navigating disconnected systems produced operational friction.
From questions to action in seconds
With Sales Assistant, sellers can interact with enterprise systems using natural language prompts. A seller preparing for a renewal can ask, "What's the renewal strategy for this account?" and receive a grounded, cited response in seconds. Another seller can request, "Generate a quote for opportunity XYZ," and the agent prepares it for human review before submission.
Instead of searching across multiple applications, sellers interact through a single interface that connects to the enterprise systems where their data already resides.
Behind the scenes, Sales Assistant orchestrates specialized sub-agents that interact with Salesforce, customer engagement platforms, pricing and configuration systems, lifecycle databases, and internal knowledge repositories. Every response is grounded in enterprise data, giving sellers visibility into the sources behind each recommendation.
Sales Assistant also maintains conversational context across multiple interactions. Sellers can ask follow-up questions like "What products is this customer currently using?" without repeating previous context, enabling a more natural and efficient workflow.
Sales Assistant fits into existing workflows. Sellers can interact with it within the tools they already use, including Salesforce, Slack, a web interface, and a mobile application.
Running in production, not in a lab
Sales Assistant is not a prototype or proof of concept. It is a production AI agent processing thousands of requests every day.
Running AI at production scale requires more than deploying an LLM. Sales Assistant is built on Red Hat AI using a layered architecture (see Figure 1) designed to deliver scalability, governance, security, and operational reliability.
Figure 1. Sales Assistant architecture diagram showing orchestration, model inference, deployment, autoscaling, and observability
Users authenticate through Red Hat’s single sign-on technology, which is based on Keycloak. After authentication, requests are routed to the Supervisor Agent running on Red Hat OpenShift AI.
The Supervisor Agent orchestrates specialized agents, manages tool execution through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers registered in the Red Hat OpenShift AI MCP registry, and coordinates access to enterprise systems with centralized governance and observability.
Red Hat AI Inference handles model inference using a hybrid strategy that automatically selects the most suitable hosted or frontier models for each request, balancing latency, performance, and cost.
To ground responses in enterprise knowledge, the platform continuously ingests documents—more than 300,000 so far—using data pipelines built with KubeRay and Docling on Red Hat OpenShift AI. This retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline grounds responses in current enterprise knowledge. At query time, the platform retrieves the most relevant information, re-ranks results using models served through Red Hat AI Inference, and injects only the highest-value context into the model prompt.
The application platform is standardized on Red Hat Universal Base Image based on Red Hat Enterprise Linux, while backend services are built with Quarkus to provide lightweight, cloud-native Java services optimized for Kubernetes.
Application promotion across development, staging, and production environments is managed through Kustomize. Horizontal Pod Autoscalers dynamically adjust capacity as demand changes, while observability provides operational visibility across the entire platform.
Helping sellers focus on customers
By bringing enterprise data and business actions together in a single conversational experience, Sales Assistant reduces the time sellers spend searching for information and navigating disconnected systems.
Sales Assistant isn’t yet another tool or system sellers need to navigate; it’s an intelligent interface for existing enterprise tools, and helps sellers prepare faster, respond with greater confidence, and spend more time focused on customer conversations.

The platform is also evolving toward more proactive and adaptive AI agents that can anticipate user needs while continuing to operate within enterprise governance, security, and compliance boundaries.
Building enterprise AI for production
Enterprises no longer have to prove that AI models are capable of doing real work. Their next challenge is to deploy AI tools that securely connect to enterprise data, integrate with business workflows, and operate reliably at scale.
Built on Red Hat AI, Sales Assistant combines orchestration, retrieval, governance, and observability into a production-ready platform for enterprise deployments.

Managing a sprawling, diverse hybrid cloud can feel like trying to schedule a meeting that works for 4 different time zones, 3 different business units, and that 1 stakeholder who is “tentatively” available. It can be really, really tedious.

Think of it as your intelligent assistant living right inside your Red Hat OpenShift web console, ready to help you tackle cluster operations (without complaining). Here are 5 ways that OpenShift Lightspeed helps you cut down manual tasks and ease the daily grind—with sample prompts.
Get context-aware answers rooted in official product documentation
Instead of spending time manually searching through thousands of pages of official product manuals, you can query OpenShift Lightspeed in plain language. The assistant acts as an intelligent, version-aware guide—analyzing the latest Red Hat documentation and factoring in the specific version of Red Hat OpenShift and Lightspeed running in your cluster to provide tailored, accurate answers directly within your console.
Examples of what you can ask:
- "How do I configure a custom ingress controller?"

OpenShift Lightspeed generates compliant, structured YAML configurations based on your specific natural language requests. This speeds up workflows and reduces manual coding errors for senior platform engineers while helping newer administrators generate valid configurations without starting from scratch.'
Examples of what you can ask:
- "Generate a YAML file for a deployment running a basic NGINX server with 3 replicas."
- "Create a YAML configuration to set up a persistent volume claim using local storage."

When a pod crashes right before end-of-day, you don’t have time to wade through thousands of log lines. OpenShift Lightspeed analyzes the errors for you and walks you through exact diagnostic steps so you can fix the issue and get back to your evening.
Examples of what you can ask:

To make that transition easier, OpenShift Lightspeed delivers intelligent assistance specifically tailored for Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization. Administrators can ask questions about migrating virtualized workloads, configuring storage, and managing VMs using familiar, straightforward language.

- “Is there a storage vMotion equivalent?"

Through cluster-interaction capabilities, OpenShift Lightspeed moves beyond generalized guidance to retrieve real-time context from your active clusters. Instead, just remember that OpenShift Lightspeed is your helper—for the tedious, mundane, repetitive work required to run a hybrid cloud. So if you’re spending your days writing YAML and reviewing logs manually, I have a better idea. Let OpenShift Lightspeed take care of those tasks while you have more fun … or at least more time.

title: Standardized, secure, and scalable: The Optus blueprint for Red Hat Enterprise Linux automation factory
full_content:
Telecom infrastructure teams often face the same bottleneck: Every new Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) server is a custom job. Images multiply. Hardening is inconsistent. Patching and compliance become manual follow-up work after the machine is already live.
If you've ever managed enterprise Linux infrastructure at scale, you know the routine. A team requests a new server, and what should be a straightforward task turns into a manual, custom build. Someone picks an outdated template, tweaks a few config files by hand, and skips a security setting to get it live on time. Months later, an audit flag pops up, and you're stuck manually retrofitting security controls on a production machine.
As custom configurations drift and template libraries balloon, keeping servers secure and patched becomes a constant fight. That was the exact bottleneck Optus set out to solve. Optus wanted a better model, one standard way to build, provision, and secure RHEL at scale, without relying on console work or one-off templates.
Working with Red Hat Consulting in Australia and New Zealand, Optus built an automated RHEL factory: A governed pipeline that delivers consistent RHEL 8 and RHEL 9 virtual machines (VMs), with Center for Internet Security (CIS) Level 1 controls applied at provision time. The factory runs on Red Hat Satellite, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, and GitLab in Optus’s environment. It's designed to extend to future RHEL versions without redesigning the operating model.
How the factory works
To move away from manual builds, the factory focuses on three guiding principles:
- Standardize: A repeatable model defines how RHEL images are created, versioned, and deployed.
- Automate: Self-service VM delivery replaces manual steps using Ansible Automation Platform for provisioning, and GitLab CI/CD to build the golden images.
- Secure: CIS Level 1 compliance is built into every VM at provision time, not added later as an audit exercise.
From Day 0 to Day 2
The factory separates image creation from provisioning and ongoing operations:
Day 0 (Image build factory): A version-selectable GitLab CI/CD pipeline works with Red Hat Enterprise Linux image builder to produce a governed open virtual appliance (OVA). The approved thin OVA is published to the enterprise VMware vCenter Content Library.
Day 1 (Provisioning and security hardening): When a team needs a new workload, an Ansible workflow runs a survey-driven deployment to VMware. Cloud-init handles first-boot configuration. Ansible Automation Platform then applies runtime hardening and baseline configuration through repeatable roles.
Day 2 and beyond (Operations and compliance): After provisioning, the VM registers to Red Hat Satellite, which provides content, patching, and lifecycle control so that compliance doesn't depend on ad hoc maintenance.
Built for real constraints
When RHEL deployments scale, infrastructure teams often face the same 3 hurdles: Image sprawl, unpredictable networking, and a Satellite model that becomes hard to manage. Optus tackled those issues directly:
- One image per RHEL version: Instead of maintaining a large template library, Optus uses one thin OVA per RHEL version. Ansible Automation Platform sizes the workload at deploy time.
- Predictable networking: A sanitization step on the image builder host addresses a known upstream limitation so networking stays consistent from first boot.
- A scalable Satellite model: Role-based access control (RBAC), standardized activation keys, uniform host groups, and layered content views keep shared base content consistent while giving teams clean separation.
Security and compliance results
Security sits in the pipeline, not after go-live. Build and publish stages are separated so approved images carry clear metadata into provisioning.
Ansible Roles and OpenSCAP validation collect evidence during deployment. Measured results for CIS Level 1 OS-conditional controls:
- RHEL 8: 97.42% compliance
- RHEL 9: 97.10% compliance
Both scores meet Optus’s 95% compliance target. The remaining items are known Optus exceptions.
The outcome
Optus now operates the full factory: GitLab pipelines for golden images, an Ansible workflow for Day 1 provisioning and hardening, and Satellite for ongoing lifecycle control, all running in Optus's own environment.
Built for what's next
With Day 0 image builds and Day 1 provisioning in place, the natural next step is Day 2 operations: Governed patching and lifecycle management through the same Satellite and Ansible Automation Platform stack.
That foundation also matters for the longer term. AI-assisted operations work best when the infrastructure underneath them is standardized: Known inventory, repeatable playbooks, approval paths, and measurable compliance. Agentic AI can sit on top of that governed automation layer so future AI-assisted capabilities direct existing workflows rather than inventing unmanaged change.

title: Make Every Paytm UPI Payment More Secure with Biometric Authentication on Paytm
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
There are some everyday moments when you realise just how much your phone does for you. Ordering food, booking a cab, splitting a bill, or making a quick payment at your favourite café can all happen in a few taps.
And now, Paytm UPI payments are getting even more convenient with biometric authentication on Paytm.
With Paytm, UPI payments can now be verified using your fingerprint on Android or Face ID on iPhone, so you don’t always have to enter your UPI PIN. It is a small change, but one that can make everyday mobile payments feel much faster and smoother.
Your Face or Fingerprint Can Verify Your Payment
We’ve all been there. You’re in a hurry, there’s a queue behind you, and you’re trying to remember your UPI PIN before the payment goes through.
With biometric authentication on Paytm, that extra step can be skipped for eligible payments up to ₹5,000. You can simply use your fingerprint or Face ID to verify the payment. For payments above ₹5,000, your UPI PIN is required. And if you prefer using your UPI PIN for an eligible payment, that option is still available.
The idea isn’t to change how you make UPI payments completely. It is simply about giving you another convenient way to verify them.
Why biometric authentication on Paytm Feels More Convenient
The biggest advantage is pretty straightforward: less friction.
Your fingerprint and Face ID are already part of how you unlock and use your phone. Bringing that familiar experience into Paytm UPI payments means you can authenticate eligible payments without manually entering your UPI PIN every time.
It can also be useful when you’re making a payment in a busy public place. Instead of entering your PIN where people around you might see your screen, biometric authentication gives you another way to verify an eligible payment.
It feels less like learning something new and more like your phone quietly getting better at something you already do every day.
Your Phone Can Also Help You Access Cash
The convenience doesn’t stop at Paytm UPI payments.
At supported ATMs, Paytm users can make cardless ATM withdrawals using UPI. Simply select the UPI Cash Withdrawal option on the ATM, scan the QR code using Paytm, and authenticate the withdrawal using Face ID, fingerprint, or your UPI PIN.
That means your phone can handle another everyday task without needing a debit card.
A Small Upgrade to Everyday Mobile Payments
Technology is most useful when it makes everyday things feel simpler without making them complicated.
Biometric authentication on Paytm does exactly that for eligible Paytm UPI payments. You get the choice of using Face ID or fingerprint for eligible payments up to ₹5,000, while your UPI PIN remains available when required.
Add cardless ATM withdrawals at supported ATMs, and your phone is becoming much more useful for everyday financial tasks.
Sometimes, the best technology upgrade is the one you barely have to think about.

title: How to Set Up Paytm Postpaid in Just a Few Minutes
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
Need a little extra flexibility for your payments? Paytm Postpaid gives you access to Credit on Paytm UPI, so you can spend now and pay next month.
Setting up Paytm Postpaid is a simple, guided process that involves checking your offer, completing KYC, setting up UPI AutoPay and creating your Paytm Postpaid UPI PIN.
Here’s a step-by-step guide to getting started.
What is Paytm Postpaid?
Paytm Postpaid is a Buy Now, Pay Later facility that gives you a short-term credit limit that you can use for payments and repay later. You can use it for both online and offline payments.
You can get a credit limit of up to ₹60,000 which may be upgraded based on your credit history and other factors.
How to Set Up Paytm Postpaid
Step 1: Open the Paytm app
Open the Paytm app on your phone.
You can find Paytm Postpaid by:
- Scrolling to the Financial Services section on the Paytm app homepage, or
- Searching for “Postpaid” using the search bar.
Tap on Paytm Postpaid to begin the setup process.
Step 2: Enter your PAN details
Enter your PAN details as prompted.
Your details will be used to evaluate your offer. Based on your credit history and other factors, you’ll see the credit limit available to you.
Step 3: Review your offer and proceed
Once your offer is displayed, read the applicable terms and conditions carefully.
If you’re happy with the offer, tap “Proceed with this offer.”
There is no signup fee for setting up Paytm Postpaid, and there is no charge simply for signing up and not using the facility.
Step 4: Complete Aadhaar verification
After you proceed with the offer, the next steps may take a few seconds to process.
You’ll then complete the verification process with Suryoday Small Finance Bank, the lending partner for Paytm Postpaid.
An OTP will be sent to the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar.
Enter the OTP and tap “Verify.”
Never share your OTP with anyone.
Next, enter your Aadhaar number, agree to the applicable terms and conditions, and tap “Perform KYC.”
Step 5: Complete your KYC and selfie verification
Your Aadhaar information will now be validated.
You may see a short processing screen while your details are being checked, followed by the selfie verification step.
When prompted, submit your selfie.
For a smoother verification:
- Make sure your face is clearly visible.
- Use a well-lit place.
- Avoid anything covering your face.
- Follow the instructions displayed on the screen.
If required, you can retake your selfie until you’re satisfied with the result.
Step 6: Give consent for credit bureau verification
You’ll then be asked to provide consent to Suryoday Small Finance Bank to collect, store and verify your credit information from different credit bureaus.
Read the consent carefully before proceeding.
The verification can take up to 60 seconds. Stay on the screen during this process and do not press back or close the app.
Once the process is complete, you’ll see confirmation that your credit line has been approved.
Step 7: Link your credit line
Once your credit line is approved, tap “Link credit line.”
You will be asked to provide some additional details, such as your email address, annual income and more. Enter the requested information and continue.
Step 8: Set up UPI AutoPay
Next, you’ll need to set up UPI AutoPay for your Paytm Postpaid repayments.
This is a required part of the setup and allows your repayments to be collected automatically when your bill is due.
During setup, ₹1 will be debited from your bank account to verify the mandate. This amount is refunded.
You may also see a ₹15,000 mandate limit on the screen. This is the maximum amount of the AutoPay mandate and does not mean that ₹15,000 will be deducted from your account. The amount collected when your bill is due will be your applicable bill amount.
Review the details, agree and proceed.
Step 9: Sign the agreement
Your details will be sent to Suryoday Small Finance Bank to complete the agreement.
Enter your Aadhaar details and tap “Send OTP.”
Enter the OTP you receive and tap “Verify.”
Your agreement will then be digitally signed.
Step 10: Set up your Paytm Postpaid UPI PIN
Your Paytm Postpaid credit line now needs its own UPI PIN.
Set it up just like you would set up a PIN for another Paytm UPI account.
You’ll be asked to complete Aadhaar verification again as part of setting up the PIN.
Once your PIN is successfully created, your Paytm Postpaid account is ready to use.
Start using Paytm Postpaid
That’s it! Your Paytm Postpaid setup is complete.
Once activated, Paytm Postpaid will appear as a payment option when you make eligible payments. It can be used for payments across millions of stores, online websites and apps that accept Paytm UPI, and eligible recharges and bill payments on the Paytm app.
With Paytm Postpaid, you can get up to ₹60,000 credit limit, enjoy up to a 45-day credit period, and pay your bill the following month.

title: Why Paytm Is Building Applied AI, Not Just Another Chatbot
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming part of everyday technology. Yet much of the conversation around AI still centres on chatbots and conversational interfaces. At Paytm, we are taking a different approach.
We are building applied AI, which is artificial intelligence designed around specific business problems, merchant workflows and consumer journeys. Rather than treating AI as a separate product layer, we are embedding intelligence into how our platform operates, from merchant onboarding and servicing to fraud prevention, collections, customer acquisition, personalisation and software development.
As highlighted in our Q1 FY 2027 earnings release, AI is now part of our core operating processes. We have developed function-specific models and agents by fine-tuning open-source models, with applications across engineering, merchants and consumers. That is the foundation of our applied AI approach, and it is already showing up in how fast the business is growing and how efficiently it is being built.
Applied AI Built Around Real Business Use Cases
Our approach to AI begins with a simple question: what business problem can technology solve better?
For merchants, we started by applying AI to onboarding, servicing and business insights through the Paytm AI Soundbox. We are now building agents that help merchants market their services, engage with customers across channels including the Paytm app, and service those customers more effectively.
AI is also becoming more relevant across our merchant financial services ecosystem. Our merchant loan distribution business uses AI-led lifecycle management of device merchants, including risk insights for lending partners and collections. In Q1 FY 2027, AI-led capabilities helped drive gains in merchant engagement, retention, risk insights for partners and collection efficiency.
Across consumers, AI-led acquisition is helping us select better-quality customers more efficiently, while AI-led personalisation is helping serve more relevant use cases and improve engagement across financial services products. The common thread is that AI is being deployed where it can influence a real operating or customer outcome.
Specialised AI Models for Indian Businesses
Applied AI also requires the right model for the job. Rather than relying only on very large general-purpose models, we are building and optimising specialised models for our own use cases.
During the Q1 FY 2027 earnings call, our Founder and CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma explained that we tune models ourselves, deploy them on our own infrastructure and optimise them for specific applications. He shared one example where a 200-billion-parameter model was optimised into a 4-billion-parameter model designed for Indian languages, and then placed on our own machines.
As Vijay Shekhar Sharma put it on the call, this means low latency, a lower cost of tokens and low running cost, operated by us. That approach makes our cost lower than it would be for a typical company, and it lets us replace expenses such as third-party call-centre costs while adding a new capability of our own.
This matters in a market like India, where businesses operate across many languages, regions and very different operating environments. For applied AI to work at scale, it needs to be fast, cost-efficient and suited to the context in which it is used. Our earlier work around the Paytm AI Soundbox follows the same philosophy, with applied AI models and smaller language models designed around small-business contexts, voice and Indian languages.
AI for Merchants and Small Businesses
India’s small-business ecosystem is one of the clearest opportunities for applied AI. A local merchant does not necessarily need another standalone technology interface. Technology needs to fit naturally into the way the business already operates.
That is why the Paytm AI Soundbox is such an important part of our AI journey. The Soundbox has evolved beyond payment confirmation into a broader merchant operating interface, bringing business information and merchant assistance to a device already present at the storefront.
In Q1 FY 2027, we had 1.57 crore merchants on subscription plans, adding 27 lakh net devices year-on-year, while merchant GMV grew 31% year-on-year to ₹7.1 lakh crore. We described the Soundbox as an indispensable operating system deployed across 1.57 crore storefronts in India. This existing distribution gives us an opportunity to bring AI-led services directly into everyday merchant workflows, rather than expecting merchants to adopt an entirely new system.
AI Across the Paytm Ecosystem
The use of AI extends well beyond merchant-facing products. Across engineering, we are using agentic assistance for coding, review, testing and deployment. As highlighted in our Q1 FY 2027 earnings release, this is helping create faster delivery cycles and lower the cost of building software, while the end-to-end development cycle is being made AI-ready across its different components.
Across consumers, AI-led acquisition helps us identify better-quality customers more efficiently, and personalisation helps serve more relevant use cases and improve engagement. Across merchants, AI is being applied to onboarding, servicing, business insights and sales workflows.
On the earnings call, Vijay Shekhar Sharma described how AI now supports our field sales workflow, with an agent helping identify what our field sales executives should do in small-business merchant acquisition, built in-house. Together, these applications reflect a broader shift, where AI is becoming part of how the business operates rather than remaining a standalone technology initiative.
AI-Led Operating Leverage
The impact of this approach is becoming visible in our operating metrics. In Q1 FY 2027, our revenue increased 28% year-on-year to ₹2,448 crore, while total indirect expenses grew by only 6%. EBITDA reached a record ₹203 crore, up 182% year-on-year, our highest ever quarterly EBITDA.
The cost of building our platform declined 3% year-on-year, from ₹749 crore to ₹729 crore. Software, cloud and data-centre expenses declined 5% to ₹159 crore, even as we continued to invest in AI. We attributed the reduction in platform-building costs in part to significant AI-led optimisation and productivity gains that helped absorb annual appraisal increments.
At the same time, we continued to invest in growth. For us, AI-led efficiency does not simply mean cutting costs. It means building operating leverage so the business can grow faster than its underlying cost base. On the earnings call, our President and Group CFO Madhur Deora noted that our EBITDA margin, adjusted for the PIDF incentive, improved from 1% to 8% year-on-year, even as we kept investing where it made sense.
From AI Efficiency to AI Monetisation
The next phase of our applied AI approach goes beyond internal productivity. During the Q1 FY 2027 earnings call, Vijay Shekhar Sharma said we are beginning to move from an AI optimisation journey towards an AI monetisation journey. He also said some of our AI products have already started generating a small amount of revenue, and that these non-payment, non-financial-services lines are an area of personal focus.
The focus is particularly on merchants and businesses. We are building AI solutions that we first deploy within our own operations and can then take to other businesses, having relied on those solutions ourselves. Management has indicated that smaller businesses and larger enterprises are likely to need different types of AI products and services.
That creates a natural progression: build for a real internal problem, improve the technology through use at scale, and then identify where the same capability can solve problems for other businesses.
Why Applied AI Matters
The value of AI will ultimately be determined by what it can do, not simply by how convincingly it can talk. For us, that means AI assisting a merchant onboarding process, helping improve collection performance, supporting better risk insights, making software development faster, delivering relevant consumer experiences, or bringing business intelligence to a merchant through the Paytm AI Soundbox. These are practical applications tied to existing workflows, products and distribution.
At Paytm, we are building AI with that purpose in mind. Not another chatbot, but intelligence applied where it can make technology more useful for merchants, consumers and businesses across India.

title: How to Buy Digital Gold & Silver on Paytm in Just a Few Taps
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
Remember the last time you thought, “I should probably start saving in gold”? Maybe you postponed it because you thought you needed a big amount. Or because buying gold meant finding a jeweler, checking prices, figuring out storage, and making time for the whole process.
Today, you can skip most of that. Gold and silver can now be bought digitally, in amounts that fit your budget, straight from your phone. Whether you’re looking to make a one-time purchase or simply want to start building a habit, getting started can take just a few taps.
Here’s how you can buy digital gold and silver on Paytm and make precious metals a little easier to fit into your everyday financial routine.
What Is Digital Gold and Silver?
Before getting started, it helps to understand what buying digital metals means.
Digital gold allows you to buy 24K gold in small quantities through a digital platform. Instead of receiving the physical metal immediately, the equivalent quantity is purchased on your behalf and securely stored in insured vaults backed by MMTC – PAMP.
The same idea applies to digital silver. You can purchase silver digitally without having to handle physical bars or coins at the time of purchase. This makes precious metals more accessible, particularly for people who want to start small rather than wait until they have enough money for a larger physical purchase.
Why Buy Gold or Silver Digitally with Paytm Gold?
One of the biggest advantages of buying digitally is convenience. You can buy gold or silver from your phone without planning a visit to a jewelery store. There is also no need to decide on jewelery designs, worry about making charges, or immediately arrange for physical storage.
More importantly, digital buying allows you to make smaller purchases. Instead of thinking, “I’ll buy gold when I have a few thousand rupees,” you can build the habit gradually. On Paytm Gold, for example, you can start your gold journey with as little as ₹21. That small starting point can make saving feel less intimidating and more achievable.
How to Buy Digital Gold on Paytm
Buying digital gold doesn’t have to involve complicated steps. Here’s a simple walkthrough.
Step 1: Open the Paytm App
Open the Paytm app on your smartphone and look for the Gold section.
Once you’re there, you’ll be able to view the current gold price and explore your buying options.
Step 2: Enter the Amount You Want to Buy
Enter the amount you want to invest based on your budget. Whether you want to start with ₹21 as a daily SIP or make a larger purchase, you can choose an amount that works for you.
The quantity of gold you receive is calculated according to the applicable live market price.
Step 3: Review the Details
Before completing your purchase, review the amount, applicable GST and other relevant charges displayed on the platform.
With digital gold, the price you pay includes the applicable costs associated with the purchase. Unlike jewellery, there are no making charges involved.
Step 4: Complete the Payment
Choose your preferred payment method available on Paytm and complete the transaction.
Once the purchase is successful, the corresponding quantity of gold is reflected digitally in your account.
That’s it. Your gold purchase is done without having to step into a jewellery store. The process is the same for the silver too.
Where Is Your Digital Gold Stored?
One common question people have about digital gold is: “If I can’t see the gold, where is it?”
With Paytm Gold, the gold purchased is backed by physical 24K gold and stored securely in vaults operated by MMTC-PAMP.
This means your digital holding represents actual gold rather than simply being a number on your screen. The gold is stored securely, while you can view and manage your holdings digitally.
Gold or Silver: Which One Should You Buy?
There isn’t a universal answer.
Gold and silver have different characteristics, and the choice depends on your financial goals, preferences and risk considerations. Gold has traditionally been associated with long-term wealth preservation, family security and important life milestones. Silver, on the other hand, has a lower price per unit and can appeal to people who want to explore precious metals with a smaller starting amount.
Some people may prefer gold, while others may want exposure to both. The important thing is to understand what you’re buying and choose an amount that fits comfortably within your overall financial plan.
You Don’t Have to Buy Only Once
Perhaps the biggest shift digital precious metals bring is the ability to turn buying into a habit. Instead of making one large purchase every few years, you can make smaller purchases regularly.
For those who prefer a structured approach, Paytm Gold also offers Gold SIPs, allowing you to invest daily, weekly or monthly. You can start a Gold SIP with as little as ₹21/daily. For example, setting aside a small amount regularly can help you build a gold holding alongside your other financial goals without having to make a large upfront purchase. It’s less about the size of one purchase and more about building consistency over time.
Keep an Eye on Gold Prices
Prices can change regularly based on several factors, including global economic conditions, interest rates, currency movements, inflation expectations and investor demand. If you’re actively buying gold, keeping track of price movements can help you stay informed.
Paytm Gold also offers features such as Price Alerts, which can help you keep an eye on gold prices without constantly checking them yourself. The goal isn’t necessarily to predict every price movement. Instead, it’s about making informed decisions and understanding the market you’re participating in.
What Happens When You Want to Sell?
Buying digital gold doesn’t mean you have to hold it indefinitely. When you decide to sell, you can initiate the sale digitally. The selling price is based on the applicable market price at the time of the transaction, while standard applicable costs are adjusted as per the platform’s terms.
Unlike buying, GST isn’t charged again on the sale transaction. The proceeds from the sale are then processed according to the applicable payment and settlement process.
A Simpler Way to Start Your Precious Metal Journey
Gold and silver don’t have to be purchases reserved only for weddings, festivals or major milestones. With digital precious metals, you can start small, buy when it suits you and manage your holdings from your phone.
Whether you’re putting ₹21 into gold to begin a new savings habit, making a one-time purchase for a future goal, or exploring digital silver, the process can be as simple as a few taps. And sometimes, that’s all it takes to turn a traditional form of saving into a modern financial habit.
Start small. Stay consistent. Let your goals grow with you.

title: Understanding the Difference Between Credit Cards and Paytm Postpaid
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
You spot something you’ve been waiting for. The sale ends in six hours. You want to buy it, but your bank balance says, “Maybe next month.”
If you already have a credit card with enough available limit, it can come in handy. But if you don’t have one, applying for a new credit card at 11 PM isn’t exactly the most practical solution. A credit card application typically involves an application, approval and issuance process, and the timeline can vary by issuer and applicant.
This is where Paytm Postpaid can offer a different kind of convenience.
Paytm Postpaid is a Buy Now, Pay Later option that gives you access to a short-term credit limit that you can use for payments through Paytm UPI and pay back later. Once your Paytm Postpaid setup is complete, you can start using the available credit at millions of stores and apps that support mobile payments.
So, how is Paytm Postpaid different from a credit card? And when does each make sense?
Let’s break it down.
Credit Cards and Paytm Postpaid: What’s the Difference?
Both credit cards and Paytm Postpaid give you access to credit instead of requiring the full amount to come directly from your bank balance at the time of payment.
But the way you access and use that credit is different.
|  | Credit Card | Paytm Postpaid | 
| How you use it | Physical or virtual credit card | Credit on Paytm UPI | 
| Where you can use it | At merchants and online platforms that accept your card network | Anywhere Paytm UPI is accepted, online or offline | 
| Payment method | Card payment | Pay using Paytm Postpaid at checkout or scan and pay using a payment QR | 
| Credit period | Depends on your card’s billing cycle and payment due date | Up to 45 days | 
| Credit limit | Set by the card issuer | Up to ₹60,000, can be increased depending on your repayment patterns and credit history | 
| Rewards | Depends on the card | Assured 50 to 10,000 Paytm Gold Coins on each payment | 
| Annual fee | Depends on the card | No signup fee or annual fee; small convenience fee applies when you use Paytm Postpaid | 
| Best suited for | Card-specific offers, travel benefits and regular credit card usage | Quick and easy access to credit whenever you need it | 
1. Paytm Postpaid is built around the way you already pay
One of the biggest differences is the payment experience.
A credit card is, naturally, built around card payments. You either enter your card details online or use your physical/virtual card at a merchant that accepts it.
Paytm Postpaid works through Credit on Paytm UPI.
That means you can use it to scan and pay at QR codes, including non-Paytm QR codes, make online payments, or use it for eligible recharges, bill payments and bookings within the Paytm app.
So instead of thinking, “Do I have my card with me?”, the experience is closer to the way you already make payments.
2. When you need credit right now, access matters
Imagine it’s 11 PM.
You’ve found a deal you want, but you don’t have enough money in your bank account. You also don’t already have a credit card.
A new credit card may not be the solution for that particular moment because you first need to apply and get approved and issued a card.
With Paytm Postpaid, you can complete the signup journey whenever you need it. Once setup, your Paytm Postpaid account can be ready to use immediately.
This makes Paytm Postpaid particularly useful for those moments when you need a little extra room before your next payday.
3. Credit Cards and Paytm Postpaid Serve Different Needs
Credit cards have their own advantages. Depending on the card, you can get rewards, cashback, travel benefits, merchant offers and other perks. They can also be useful for larger purchases or regular spending where you want to build a credit history and make use of card-specific benefits.
Paytm Postpaid, on the other hand, is built around a different need: quick, convenient access to short-term credit when you’re making a payment through Paytm UPI.
So while a credit card can be a great option when you want card-specific benefits, Paytm Postpaid is especially useful when you want to make a mobile payment without using the money in your bank account right away.
Whether it’s an unexpected expense, an end-of-month money crunch or a sale that’s about to end, Paytm Postpaid gives you another way to pay now and pay later.
4. Paytm Postpaid brings credit to mobile payments
This is where Paytm Postpaid stands apart.
You don’t need to think of it as a replacement for your credit card. Think of it as another way to access short-term credit when you’re making a mobile payment.
With Paytm Postpaid, you can use your available credit to:
- Scan and pay at ANY payment QR code
- Make payments on the Paytm app like electricity bill, mobile recharge, and more.
- And because it works on Paytm UPI infrastructure, you can use it across both online and offline payment situations.
5. The repayment timelines work differently
Credit cards usually work around a monthly billing cycle. You make purchases during the cycle, receive a statement and then have a payment due date. The exact number of interest-free days depends on where your purchase falls within the billing cycle and the card’s terms.
Paytm Postpaid offers up to 45 days of credit. For example, a payment made on the 1st of the month can be payable by the 14th of the following month, depending on the applicable billing cycle.
That can make it useful when you’re managing expenses between two paydays.
6. What about fees?
This is one area where you should always read the terms before using any form of credit.
Credit cards can have annual or joining fees depending on the card. They can also have interest and late-payment charges if you don’t repay according to the card’s terms.
With Paytm Postpaid, there is no fee for signing up, and there is no fee if you sign up but don’t use it. When you use Paytm Postpaid, a convenience fee may apply at bill generation, ranging from 0-4% plus GST, as applicable. Late-payment and mandate-bounce charges can also apply.
In other words, whether you’re using a credit card or Paytm Postpaid, knowing the charges and repayment terms is just as important as knowing your available credit.
So, Which One Should You Use?
It doesn’t have to be an either-or decision.
A credit card can make sense when you want card-specific rewards, cashback, travel benefits, merchant offers or simply prefer paying by card.
Paytm Postpaid can make sense when you want the convenience of short-term credit while making payments through Paytm UPI.
And when the situation is: “I need to make this payment now, but my bank balance isn’t enough”, having Credit on Paytm UPI as an option can give you the flexibility to pay now and pay later.
Paytm Postpaid: Credit on Paytm UPI
With a credit limit of up to ₹60,000 and up to 45 days of credit, Paytm Postpaid gives you another way to manage short-term expenses
Terms, fees, credit limit and availability are subject to applicable eligibility and offer terms. Paytm Postpaid is a credit product and users should review the applicable terms before using it.

title: Saving for a Wedding or New Home? Here’s How Paytm Gold SIPs Make It Easier
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
Life rarely gives us just one financial goal at a time. You may be planning your wedding, thinking about buying your first home, saving for a family vacation, or simply trying to build a stronger financial future. The difficult part is not always knowing what you want to achieve. It is figuring out how to save for all of it without feeling overwhelmed.
When there are multiple dreams on your list, putting all your savings into one place can make it difficult to understand how much you are actually setting aside for each goal. This is where having a more structured approach to saving can make a difference.
With Paytm Gold SIPs, you can create separate savings for different goals and build your gold savings around what matters to you. Whether it is your wedding, your dream home, your next big trip, or another personal milestone, you can give each goal its own savings journey while starting with an amount as small as ₹21.
Why Saving for Multiple Goals Can Feel Difficult
Think about the financial goals you may have over the next few years. Perhaps you are preparing for your wedding while also hoping to make a down payment for a house. At the same time, you may want to keep some money aside for travel or create a long-term financial cushion.
When everything is important, it can be tempting to put all your savings into one common fund. But over time, this can make it difficult to know whether you are actually making enough progress towards each goal.
For example, if you have ₹50,000 saved, how much of it is really meant for your wedding? How much can you use for your home? And what happens when an unexpected expense comes up?
This is why separating your savings according to your goals can make the process easier to understand. Instead of looking at your savings as one large number, you can look at them as smaller steps towards specific milestones.
Turn Your Big Dreams Into Separate Savings Goals
A wedding and a home may both require significant amounts of money, but they are very different goals. One may be closer, while the other could be several years away. Your approach to each goal can therefore be different as well.
This is the idea behind SIPs on Paytm Gold. You can create multiple SIPs and associate them with different goals, allowing you to build separate saving habits instead of putting everything into one pool.
For instance, you could have one SIP dedicated to your wedding and another for your future home. You could even create another one for a vacation or a long-term personal goal. Each SIP/ saving can become a small, consistent step towards something specific.
This approach can make saving feel less like a large financial burden and more like a collection of manageable habits.
You Don’t Need a Large Amount to Get Started
One of the biggest reasons people postpone saving is the belief that they need a significant amount of money to make a meaningful start. When a goal such as buying a home or planning a wedding involves lakhs of rupees, putting aside a few hundred rupees can seem insignificant.
But every large financial goal begins somewhere.
With Paytm Gold, you can start investing in 24K digital gold from just ₹21 daily. You can choose to invest daily, weekly, or monthly based on what works for your saving habit. The objective is not to suggest that ₹21 alone will fund a wedding or buy a house. Rather, it is about making the first step easier and building consistency over time.
A small amount that you can comfortably set aside today can be the beginning of a much larger saving habit tomorrow.
Why Gold Can Be Part of Your Savings Journey
Gold has always held a special place in Indian households. It is associated with important occasions, family traditions, security and long-term value. Weddings, festivals and milestones often bring gold into our lives in one form or another.
Today, buying gold does not necessarily mean waiting until you have enough money to purchase jewellery or a physical gold coin. Digital gold provides another way to participate in gold ownership in smaller amounts.
With Paytm Gold, you can buy 24K gold from MMTC-PAMP at the live market price directly through your phone. The gold you purchase is stored in MMTC-PAMP vaults, which means you do not have to worry about physically storing it at home.
Keep an Eye on Gold Prices With Price Alerts
If gold is part of your savings strategy, staying aware of price movements can also be useful. Gold prices can change based on several factors, including global economic conditions, interest rates, currency movements and market sentiment.
Paytm Gold’s Price Alerts feature allows you to set an alert for a price level and receive a notification when gold reaches it. This means you can stay updated without having to constantly check the price yourself. It is one more way Paytm Gold can make the digital gold experience more convenient as you build your savings habit.

title: Common Myths About Paytm Postpaid You Should Stop Believing
source: A Comprehensive Guide to Money Transfer, Recharges, Bill Payments and Other Digital Payments | Paytm Blog
full_content:
Credit often gets a bad reputation.
For many people, the moment they hear words like credit, BNPL or Pay Later, they think of debt, hidden charges or complicated financial products. And while credit should always be used responsibly, avoiding it altogether isn’t necessarily the answer.
The reality is simple: credit is a financial tool. How you use it matters more than simply having it.
Paytm Postpaid, with Credit on Paytm UPI, is designed to give you access to short-term credit for payments when you need it, with up to 45 days of credit period.
So, before you write off Paytm Postpaid based on something you heard, let’s clear up some of the most common myths around digital credit and BNPL.
Myth 1: Using credit is always a bad thing
Reality: Responsible credit use can be a good thing.
Credit isn’t inherently good or bad. It depends on how you use it.
When you use a credit product responsibly and make your repayments on time, you’re demonstrating healthy credit behaviour. Over time, responsible use of credit can contribute to building a good credit history.
The key is to borrow only when you need to and repay on time. With Paytm Postpaid, you can spend now and repay later, with a credit period of up to 45 days.
Think of credit as a tool and not extra income.
Myth 2: BNPL means you can spend without worrying about repayment
Reality: Buy Now, Pay Later means you have to in fact pay later.
The “Pay Later” part doesn’t mean “pay whenever you want.”
Paytm Postpaid gives you access to a short-term credit limit, which needs to be repaid as per the billing and repayment terms. Late payment and mandate bounce charges can apply, so timely repayment is important.
The smartest way to use BNPL is to think ahead: If I can comfortably repay this later, does it make sense to use credit for it now?
Myth 3: You need a huge credit limit to make Paytm Postpaid useful
Reality: Your credit limit is simply the amount of credit available to you.
Paytm Postpaid can offer a credit limit of up to ₹60,000, but you don’t need to use the entire amount.
In fact, using only what you need and being consistent with repayments is a much better approach than treating your available limit as money you have to spend.
Your Paytm Postpaid credit limit may exceed ₹60,000 over time based on usage patterns and timely repayment, although such upgrades aren’t guaranteed.
Myth 4: Paytm Postpaid only works for certain payments
Reality: Credit on Paytm UPI can be used across a wide range of payments.
Paytm Postpaid can be used at millions of stores and works across online and offline payments on any payment QR codes. It can also be used for eligible recharges, bill payments and bookings on the Paytm app.
So, it isn’t limited to one type of purchase or one particular merchant network.
Myth 5: Using Paytm Postpaid means you need to keep money in your bank account
Reality: Paytm Postpaid is designed to provide credit on Paytm UPI.
One of the key features of Paytm Postpaid is that payments can be made using the Postpaid credit line rather than your available bank balance. This can be particularly useful when a necessary payment comes up before your next salary or when your cash flow is temporarily tight.
That doesn’t mean you should spend beyond your means. It simply gives you another payment option when you need some breathing room.
Myth 6: Signing up means you’ll immediately start paying charges
Reality: Signing up doesn’t automatically mean you’re charged for using the service.
There is no signup fee, and there is no fee simply for signing up and not using Paytm Postpaid. However, when you do use Postpaid, a convenience fee may apply at bill generation, along with applicable GST. Late payment and mandate bounce charges may also apply.
In other words, don’t confuse no signup fee with no charges under any circumstances. Always check the applicable terms before accepting and using a credit product.
Myth 7: Having a credit product automatically hurts your credit history
Reality: The way you manage credit matters.
Simply having access to a credit product isn’t the same as mismanaging credit.
Responsible credit behaviour such as borrowing within your means and making repayments on time is important when building and maintaining a healthy credit history. On the other hand, repeatedly missing repayments or taking on more credit than you can comfortably repay can work against you.
That’s why the goal shouldn’t be to avoid credit at all costs. It should be to understand credit and use it responsibly.
Myth 8: Paytm Postpaid is just another way to spend more
Reality: It can be a way to manage short-term cash flow but only when used thoughtfully.
There will be times when an essential payment comes up at an inconvenient point in the month. Your salary might still be a few days away, or an unexpected expense might have arrived just when your monthly budget is running low.
That’s where short-term credit can provide some flexibility.
Paytm Postpaid gives you access to Credit on Paytm UPI for payments, with up to 45 days of credit period.
But the golden rule remains: use credit for what you can repay, not for what you can’t afford.
The bottom line: Credit isn’t the problem. Unplanned credit is.
It’s understandable to be cautious about credit. But being cautious doesn’t have to mean being afraid of it.
A good credit habit is about knowing what you’re borrowing, understanding the applicable charges and repayment terms, spending within your means and paying on time.
Paytm Postpaid brings Credit on Paytm UPI to payments across online, offline and Paytm app experiences.
So the next time you hear that “credit is bad” or “BNPL is something to stay away from,” remember: the real difference is how responsibly you use it.
Once you separate the myth from the mechanics, Postpaid is simpler than it sounds: familiar UPI payments, a bit of breathing room when you need it, and a straightforward way to pay it back.
Ready to see how Paytm Postpaid works? Open the Paytm app and explore Credit on Paytm UPI.

title: As AI Increases Demands on Memory, Storage Steps Up
full_content:
Surging AI demands are driving the need for massive datasets and context windows that burst past the confines of system memory.
But rising needs aren’t met by simply adding more storage capacity. What’s needed is useful, grounded insights from AI factories and efficient, secure storage architectures that enable those insights.
At this week’s Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) conference, NVIDIA is unveiling new storage advancements and showcasing how the next leap in AI depends as much on the storage infrastructure feeding accelerated computing as on the computing power itself.
The pressure on that infrastructure is intensifying as AI agents consume massive amounts of data — and GPUs can now initiate storage requests directly, generating thousands of concurrent operations.
To serve those requests, storage systems must continuously encrypt, compress, verify and reconstruct data. These critical data services can become bottlenecks when thousands of agents access storage simultaneously.
Benchmarks highlighted in this NVIDIA technical blog show that the NVIDIA Vera CPU, part of NVIDIA Vera BlueField-4 STX, delivers up to 3.21x higher throughput than an x86 CPU in a two-stage compression and encryption pipeline. This means that with Vera, storage platforms can absorb the flood of AI data more efficiently — delivering greater throughput with significantly less compute infrastructure.
With accelerated computing, storage stops being a passive place to keep data and becomes an active part of the data path.
This upends the old economics of determining when data belongs in memory (where applications can fetch it faster) versus on a storage drive (where it can be held in cheap and plentiful space). The tradeoff was first framed 40 years ago, when the answer was measured in accessing that data in minutes. On today’s GPUs, paired with AI storage solutions from NVIDIA and partners, the same tradeoff now plays out in microseconds.
Closing the gap between AI’s needs and memory shortage depends on extreme codesign across the whole ecosystem, from memory and storage manufacturers to the software built on them.
Open Source NVIDIA cuFile APIs Enable Interoperability for Storage Solutions
At FMS, NVIDIA announced it is open sourcing its cuFile application programming interfaces (APIs) — and the vertical storage software stack underneath them — which let GPUs, not just CPUs, read from and write to storage directly. cuFile is an open source component of NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage.
Using hundreds of thousands of GPU threads, fast high-bandwidth memory and other methodologies, cuFile enables securely accessing data from storage in just microseconds.
This represents how the industry is unifying a security-first storage stack based on Linux best practices, providing interoperability between GPUs and data.
In addition, fast, secure access to data and storage is a foundational element to powering preventive and detective cybersecurity measures. Making cuFile openly available will help make security context, data and storage accessible at the speed AI-powered defenses need. Such open technologies support initiatives such as the new Open Secure AI Alliance.
This site is the new home for APIs that are open to contributions — with Google, Intel, NVIDIA and Meta as inaugural maintainers — and can be optimized for use across various software and hardware platforms, driving innovation and efficiency for developers and enterprises.
NVIDIA and Industry Leaders Advance New Frontier of AI Storage
In addition, NVIDIA and storage industry leaders are optimizing memory and storage solutions through an initiative called Storage-Next. The NVIDIA-driven initiative brings together storage makers, controller vendors, thermal design, cooling and orchestration operators, and standards bodies to align on how GPU-driven storage should behave — then turn these advancements into interoperable, open industry standards.
Storage-Next includes over 40 leading storage and flash vendors — including DDN, KIOXIA and Micron — each contributing to the next generation of AI storage technologies with NVIDIA.
The initiative is grounded in accelerated data access for large AI datasets. To support this, NVIDIA offers SCADA — short for scaled, accelerated data access — a framework that lets massively parallel GPUs pull only the data necessary for the application directly from storage into their own high-speed memory.
For example, DDN is integrating SCADA with Infinia, its software-defined, AI-native data intelligence platform built to eliminate storage bottlenecks at scale.
“AI success will be defined not by how much infrastructure organizations own, but by how productively they use it,” said Sven Oehme, chief technology officer at DDN. “Our collaboration with NVIDIA is helping create a more direct, efficient connection between GPUs and data — keeping accelerated computing resources productive, speeding time to insight and enabling customers to achieve stronger business and financial returns from their AI investments.”
Storage-Next and SCADA extend NVIDIA’s longstanding work on AI storage infrastructure, including on NVIDIA Vera BlueField-4 STX — a modular, rack-scale foundation powered by the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, NVIDIA Vera BlueField-4 storage processors and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking.
Defining a new class of AI-native data platforms, NVIDIA STX uses the unified NVIDIA DOCA security stack to let enterprises enable continuous policy enforcement in the AI data path.
Plus, NVIDIA CMX Context Memory Storage provides an AI‑native context tier for long‑context, multi‑turn, agentic AI inference, built on NVIDIA STX.
SCADA Enables Fast AI Storage That Stays Secure
Speed at the storage layer comes with a catch. Letting an application talk straight to a drive is quick, but done carelessly, it can scribble over other processes’ memory — a security hole, not a feature.
NVIDIA SCADA uses a safe, robust method to achieve scaled direct access by splitting the job in two:
- 
The user parts of an application that need raw speed stay outside the trusted computing base.
- 
A separate, privileged component configures protected access between the user application and its approved storage at setup, adhering to standard Linux protocols for security enforcement while efficiently safeguarding data.
It’s all part of how advancements in fast, massively parallel, efficient, secure AI storage infrastructure can feed better data to applications and AI factories — so they can produce more useful, accurate, grounded intelligence at scale.
